docs.title: API tool
docs.text:
Pro feature: API Explorer requires the API Tool feature in the QReports license. It is included with the applicable Pro/Premium package and can also be licensed separately. Use QRep > Settings > License Status to see the enabled features.

API Web builds, tests, previews, and saves reusable API connections and endpoint definitions. The current ribbon button opens the WebView workspace; the previous API Explorer remains under Legacy tools for comparison. Its return route goes through Query Web so the definition can use the same parameters and Excel output logic as other QReports sources.

Saved connections and APIs are grouped in the collapsible left pane. The centre contains the request method, connection, path, request tabs, and a vertically resizable response area. The right details pane contains connection-level settings. Both side panes can be collapsed and resized.

The workspace, request controls, menus and output states follow the selected QReports application theme.

docs.title: Normal workflow
docs.text:
1. Open QRep > API tool or open API Explorer from Query Tool or Canvas.
  2. Select an existing API definition or choose New.
  3. Choose a connection and enter the method, base URL, and path.
  4. Configure authentication, headers, query parameters, and an optional request body.
  5. Select Send.
  6. Inspect Data, Raw response, Submitted request, JSON request, and processing messages.
  7. Configure flattening, filtering, pagination, or looping when required.
  8. Save the API definition.
  9. Choose To Querytool to finish the Excel report definition.

docs.title: Connection and request
docs.text:
The connection contains reusable connection-level information, including optional default parameters. The API request contains the endpoint-specific method, relative path, request values, result handling, and optional API-specific parameter defaults.

Setting Purpose Connection Selects the saved connection used by the request. Method HTTP method required by the endpoint. BaseURL Connection-level service address. Path Relative endpoint path. AUTH Selects the authentication method.

Supported authentication choices include None, API Key, Bearer Token, Authorization Token Workflow, Azure Function Key, and Basic Auth. The fields displayed below AUTH change with the selected method.

Do not include real tokens, passwords, or production URLs in screenshots or shared example workbooks. Use the connection and authentication settings approved by your organization.

docs.title: Request tabs
docs.text:
Tab Use Headers Adds HTTP header key/value pairs. Query Adds URL query-string key/value pairs. Body Sends Raw, GraphQL, or Form URL Encoded content. Settings Controls flattening, postfilter, timeout, raw preview limit, and grid record limit. Pagination Repeats a request by next-link or offset rules. Loop Runs the request for values returned by another query.

Body modes are None, Raw, GraphQL, and Form Url Encoded. Raw bodies support JSON, text, XML, and JavaScript content formats. GraphQL provides separate query and variables editors.

Right-click the Headers or Query grids to remove a line, clear all lines, toggle a line, add common values, or select columns discovered in a response.

docs.title: Parameters in requests
docs.text:
QReports parameters can be used in the path, query values, headers, body, and GraphQL variables. For example:

/sales/{{pyear}}/{{region}}

Use formatted parameter output where quoting or multi-value syntax is needed. Review the submitted request in Sent and avoid logging secrets. See Parameters.

Select Connection parameters in the connection details pane to define defaults shared by every saved API under that connection. Select API parameters in the header to define defaults used only by the current API. Save the connection after changing connection parameters, and save the API after changing API parameters.

At execution time, matching names are resolved case-insensitively in this order:

  1. connection parameters provide the shared defaults;
  2. API parameters override matching connection defaults for that endpoint;
  3. parameters supplied by Excel, Canvas, or Query Workspace override both for that run.

For example, a connection can store company = 2, one API can override it to 3, and a workbook can run the same API with company = 1. If the caller supplies no company, the API default is used; if the API has no override, the connection default is used. Caller values are execution-only and are never saved back into the connection or API.

This model is useful when several APIs share tenant, company, environment, or date defaults. It also keeps a saved API runnable from a workbook or Canvas that does not define every optional parameter.

docs.title: Submit and inspect the response
docs.text:
Select Submit to execute the current request.

Response tab What it shows Submitted request The method, URL, headers, query values, and body sent to the server, without QReports wrapper metadata. JSON request The request definition represented as JSON. Raw response The returned response body before tabular conversion. Data Rows and columns produced from the response. Its column menu supports sorting, formats, aliases, visibility, and exclusions.

When a successful response produces no displayable table rows, API Explorer selects Raw so messages, scalar responses, error details, or unexpected JSON shapes remain visible. Show table reruns the table conversion using the current flattening settings.

Aliases and excluded-column lists accept one entry per line or comma-separated entries. Use source name=alias for names that contain spaces or punctuation; saved response shaping preserves those complete source names, including CSV-style result headings.

docs.title: Flattening and postfilter
docs.text:
APIs often return nested objects or arrays. Flattening selects the array that represents records and expands properties into columns. Use Flattening help to inspect the response and choose a path rather than guessing it.

Settings include:

  • preferred array property, often value;
  • flattening paths and selected result columns;
  • postfilter applied after the response has been converted;
  • API record limit for the Grid preview;
  • Raw preview limit;
  • request timeout.

Always verify the Raw response when expected fields are missing from Grid. The API may have changed its wrapper or nesting even though the request itself succeeded.

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text:
Enable pagination when one request returns only part of the available data.

Type Use Next link Reads the next request URL or token from a response property. Offset Advances offset/limit values until the stop condition or maximum page count is reached.

Configure the data property containing rows, start offset, page size, maximum pages, and optional page-number output column. Set conservative limits while testing.

docs.title: Loop requests
docs.text:
Loop mode runs the API request once for each value returned by a source query. The loop query can be built through Query Tool and can supply tokens used in the path, query parameters, headers, body, or GraphQL variables.

Loop settings include connection, source query, value column, token name, maximum requests, delay, empty-value handling, and optional loop value/index columns. Pagination is applied inside each loop request.

Start with a small maximum request count. Confirm the API's rate limits and acceptable-use rules before running a large loop.

docs.title: Save and manage definitions
docs.text:
• Save stores the current named API definition.
  • Api definitions opens the manager where definitions can be loaded, renamed, duplicated, or deleted.
  • Export to postman file and Import postman file exchange supported request definitions with Postman-format files.
  • New clears the editor for a new request.

docs.title: Return through Query Tool
docs.text:
Choose To Querytool after the response structure is correct.

Query Tool receives the API JSON definition, endpoint path, and preview table. From there you can:

  • inspect and rename columns;
  • add QReports parameters;
  • add Mini DAX measures or calculated columns;
  • choose the Excel output type;
  • return or patch the definition into the active worksheet.

If the existing Excel definition contains measures and the API result does not provide replacements, Query Tool preserves the stored measure definition and displays a warning. This prevents an API edit from silently deleting existing report measures.

Continue with Query Tool, Parameters, or Mini DAX and measures.

docs.title: Standalone request JSON with BaseUrl
docs.text:
Use BaseUrl instead of Connection when a request (including a token workflow request) does not need a saved connection:

{
  "Type": "api",
  "BaseUrl": "https://api.example.com",
  "Method": "POST",
  "Path": "auth/token",
  "BodyMode": 1,
  "ContentType": "application/json",
  "Headers": {},
  "Body": "{\"clientId\":1,\"tenantId\":\"example\",\"apiKey\":\"{{secret:MyApiKey}}\"}"
}

Path is relative to BaseUrl; it can be empty if BaseUrl is the complete endpoint address. BaseUrl must be an absolute HTTP/HTTPS URL without embedded credentials, query parameters or fragments. Put query parameters in Query.

With BaseUrl, no connection is created or saved, and no saved authentication or default headers are inherited. Supply required headers/body values in the JSON. If both BaseUrl and Connection are present, BaseUrl takes precedence and the saved connection is ignored, preventing its credentials from being forwarded to another host. Omit BaseUrl to retain the existing Connection behavior. Secret references in request text are resolved normally; keep actual API keys/passwords in Secrets, not literal JSON.

In Authentication → Token workflow → API request JSON, paste this request into Token request JSON and set the token JSON path to the property returned by that API, such as accessToken. The main API connection remains separate from this standalone token request.

Query parameters and Headers are separate, full-width collapsible groups under Parameters. Expand either group to edit its key/value rows.

Right-click a Data cell, Raw response, Submitted request or JSON request to Copy details, Copy all, or Clear this view. Copy details uses the selected text or clicked cell; Copy all in Data copies the structured result as JSON. Clear is local to that output view and does not delete a saved API definition. Clearing JSON request while Manual JSON is on means you must provide valid JSON before sending.

API URLs in Data and Raw response are clickable. Click a link, or right-click Open as API request… (relative URLs can also be selected). The workspace keeps the current connection and prepares a GET request for review; nothing runs until you click Send. Pagination and request loops are disabled for this one-off request. Use Back to restore the previous request and response. Only URLs on the same origin as the current connection are accepted, preventing credentials from being forwarded to a different API. Turn Manual JSON off before using this navigation.

docs.title: Graphics and layout
docs.text: Graphics add structure and explanation without requiring a datasource. Qanvas supports formatted text, lines, rectangles, ovals, connectors, images, and SVG content alongside normal tiles.

docs.title: Graphics
docs.text:
• Text graphics support the same rich-text concepts as Text tiles and Gantt descriptions: headings, colors, bullets, checklists, links, editable tables, code/diagram blocks, and compressed inline images.
  • Use safe formatted HTML in a Text tile or Text graphic for a one-off, mostly static composition such as outlined callouts, boxes with arrows, code panels, or a simple flow diagram. Use SVG instead when geometry must scale precisely or bind to data, separate canvas shapes and connectors when parts must remain independently movable, and Multi-card for a repeated data-driven layout.
  • Insert > Date countdown adds date-driven text without a datasource or measure. Choose a target date and configure separate text for a future date, the target day, and a passed date. Use {days} for the absolute number of days or {date} for the formatted target date. While editing, it remains a readable and copyable function such as datecountdown("2026-10-11", "Neste om {days}", "I dag", "Ferdig"). The dialog formats it as a subtle wrapping code chip. Normal, presentation, and exported views show only the recalculated result.
  • Selecting an inline image opens an image-only floating toolbar above or below it. Set width, align left/center/right, compress, remove, or drag a corner handle while preserving aspect ratio. Clicking text returns to text editing.
  • Lines and shapes support color, thickness, solid/dotted/dashed styles, transparency, fill, rounding, movement, and resizing.
  • Connectors attach to tile edges and follow the connected tiles when they move.
  • Connector routing, endpoints, arrow size, line style, and layer order are configurable.
  • Pictures and SVG graphics can be embedded so the report remains portable.
  • Custom SVG created from source uses the Manual template. In document JSON, keep the standalone element only in nested svgGraphic.svgCode and explicitly set nested svgGraphic.template to lowercase manual.
  • Open SVG designer… shows a collapsible reusable-template gallery and a full Custom SVG workspace. Analyze SVG discovers text components, editable shapes, likely category labels and a horizontal date axis with a Today/I dag marker. Detected text can be edited in place with font, size, weight, color and link controls; named shapes expose fill, border, border width, position and supported geometry. Paired horizontal rectangles are recognized as a progress track and fill even without field metadata, so the fill width can be changed directly in Progress fill > Position and size. Explicit data-qanvas-field and data-qanvas-label attributes remain the most reliable choice for other editable shapes. Use as category slot is separate from editing: only checked slots are filled, in order, with unique values from the selected source column. The date marker can follow the current date, a fixed date, a source field or a parameter between a configured start and end date. Click a detected item in the preview to open, scroll to, and highlight its controlling component or date-marker editor. Duplicate copies normal components, while Duplicate marker copies the label, badge and line and adds an independently configured dynamic marker rather than only cloning its text. The preview uses the same tile frame and render path as the applied graphic, including the final tile aspect ratio. Raw SVG source, component editing, colors and data bindings all live in the designer rather than being duplicated in Properties. Right-click an editable text or date-label input, or use its ＋ insert button, to open the searchable field/measure/parameter token lookup. The catalog includes related-source measures when relationships make them available to the SVG tile.
  • CanvasWeb/examples/manual-svg-timeline.svg is a complete editable timeline example with month/week labels, category lanes, a Today marker, theme colors and named components.

docs.title: Multi-card tiles
docs.text:
Use Add tile > Multi-card when the same small information layout should be repeated for countries, projects, milestones, customers, or another dimension. Open the designer and choose a Group by column. Add any number of source fields or measures to the Values well and arrange them in one to six columns. Raw source fields support First, Sum, Average, Min, Max, and Count; measures are evaluated in the filter context of each repeated card.

Each value column can use Auto / remaining, Percent, or Fixed width. Auto columns share space that remains after fixed-pixel columns. Percentage values act as responsive proportions and are normalized with the Auto columns; for example, 15% + Auto + 25% produces a 15 / 60 / 25 layout. Prefer percent/Auto for presentation layouts that must resize, and use fixed pixels only for compact columns such as dates, icons, or status labels.

Each value also has a Placement section. Leave Column on Auto flow for the normal left-to-right layout, or pin an image, data bar, or other value to a numbered column. Height can occupy one to six rows or the Full column; the remaining values flow densely through the other available cells. For example, use two value columns, pin an image to column 1 with Full column height, and leave three text values on Auto flow to stack them in column 2.

The value's Align setting applies to both its value and caption. Open Cell display on a value to render it as a number/text value, image, badge, icon, or data bar. Badge and icon colors can follow a theme role, indicate positive/negative status, or use a custom color. Each value also exposes the same Data bar / bullet graph and Conditional formatting controls used by table and matrix columns, including comparison fields/measures, value-strength colors, negative-value color, emphasis and threshold icons. Format using can point to a different numeric field or measure while the displayed value remains text; for example, show date_diff while colors are calculated from date_diff_days. A value can also drive a thin card Color band on the left, right, top, or bottom edge. The band can use the conditional result or a separate field/measure that returns a hex color or theme role.

Heading and supporting-text templates support {{group}}, {{field:Amount|Sum}}, {{measure:Sales}}, and {{parameter:Year}}. Card captions support the same tokens. Right-click a heading, supporting-text, or caption input to insert a field, measure, parameter, group value, or the upper/lower text functions without typing the token. The menu also inserts an editable datecountdown(...) expression using today's date as a starting point. Each value initially shows only its field/measure, aggregation and caption; open More for format, alignment, placement, cell display, data bars and conditional formatting. Card placement uses CSS grid with either a fixed number of cards per row or an automatic minimum width. Use Show heading instead of an empty or whitespace heading when only supporting text is needed. In the designer preview, click a heading, supporting text, value, or value caption to scroll to and focus its corresponding setting. Text and number boxes update the preview when focus leaves the box, avoiding a full preview refresh for every typed character; selects, checkboxes, and color controls remain immediate. Colors and borders may inherit the Qanvas theme or be set explicitly. No background (transparent) removes the repeated cards' fill while retaining theme-based text and accent colors. Border sides can show all edges, only the top and vertical sides, only horizontal separators, or no inner card border. Border width supports fractional values such as 0.25 and 0.5 px for subtle dividers. Use a Multi-card rather than a rich-text table when rows must be generated dynamically from data; use a rich-text table for a small, manually authored piece of narrative content.

When a Multi-card is selected on the canvas, Up Arrow and Down Arrow scroll its card body when it overflows. The same behavior applies to a long Text box configured for internal scrolling.

docs.title: Arrange a page
docs.text:
Use alignment guides for visual placement and the Properties pane for exact coordinates and dimensions. Multi-selection is useful for moving, aligning, copying, or deleting a group of objects. Hide design handles and type tags when reviewing the finished layout.

Pages support preset or manual dimensions, including widescreen presentation and A4 portrait, plus page colors and background images. Tiles can use rounded corners, transparent surfaces, optional borders, and explicit layer ordering. Text objects clip at the box edge by default for a clean canvas. Choose Scroll inside box for long, webpage-like content; editing follows the same scroll container.

docs.title: Themes
docs.text:
The Canvas theme controls page and visual roles such as surface, text, headers, grid lines, and data-series palettes. Individual visuals can inherit the theme or use explicit overrides. Keeping theme roles separate from chart-series colors makes a report easier to restyle consistently.

See the complete Canvas reference and then configure Presentation and sharing.

docs.title: Presentation and sharing
docs.text: Qanvas Presentation mode shows the report without design controls while keeping navigation, zoom, filters, pointer, and temporary annotation tools available.

docs.title: Navigate and zoom
docs.text:
• Right Arrow opens the next page; Left Arrow opens the previous page.
  • Double-click a tile to animate into a focused view.
  • While a tile is focused, double-click it again, press Escape, or press Left Arrow to return to the exact prior zoom and scroll position.
  • Each page can open with Automatic, Fit screen, Fit width, Fit height, or 100% resizing. Automatic uses Fit screen for known slide presets and Fit width for manual, A4, and long web/report pages.
  • Ctrl + mouse wheel zooms the Qanvas page around the pointer. Drag to pan a zoomed page.
  • Full screen hides the application title bar. Press F11 to enter full screen and press F11 again to leave it; the toolbar action and Escape remain available as alternatives.
  • Use B to enter or leave a black screen.

Presentation settings retain the report-level viewer preferences and animation choice. Moving to another page reapplies that page's resize choice. Page tabs stay in the compact top row while space remains; additional pages move into the … menu instead of creating a scrollbar or a second toolbar row. Zoom and Annotations are collapsed menus, and their complete button surface opens the menu.

Controls can auto-hide or remain pinned. Auto-hidden controls are an overlay, so showing or hiding them does not resize or move the report. Pinning the controls reserves toolbar space and resizes the presentation area deliberately. The page counter and slide chooser help with larger reports.

docs.title: Pointer and annotations
docs.text:
The red pointer can remain active independently of drawing. Rectangle and oval annotations are stored separately for each page during the presentation. Use Undo, the eraser, or Clear page to remove them. Ctrl+Z removes the latest annotation. All temporary annotations are discarded when Presentation mode closes.

Right-click the presentation for slide navigation, full/black screen, pointer, fit options, annotations, slide chooser, and filters without first opening the top controls. Press F to show or hide the filter panel; the shortcut is also available in an exported webpage when filters are enabled for its profile.

docs.title: Exit safely
docs.text: Return to edit closes directly. Escape first leaves black screen, full screen, or tile focus as applicable. Once back at the normal page view, Escape asks before closing Presentation mode so the current position and annotations are not lost accidentally.

docs.title: Inheriting and locking filters
docs.text:
Presentation profiles and web exports use Inherit filters from editor by default. With this option enabled, configured source and page filters become viewer controls and open with the same values and filter type used in the canvas editor. Page filters retain their page scope instead of being promoted to report-wide filters. Separate filters that use the same datasource column retain their own stable IDs instead of being merged. This lets a visual filter configured to Follow filter type remain single-select when its linked filter is a Dropdown or another single-selection type. Changing a viewer control replaces that inherited value for the presentation session; returning to edit restores the saved editor value.

Use Lock filter on a source, page, or tile filter when it is an authored report constraint. Locked filters remain active, but their columns are omitted from presentation and exported-web filter controls. Turn inheritance off to use the existing advanced manual filter-column setup for that profile instead.

docs.title: Webpage reports
docs.text:
Web exports preserve the same compact page overflow menu, collapsible zoom and annotation controls, auto-hide overlay behavior, fit and zoom behavior, tile focus, filters, and report appearance settings. A folder export contains the complete website; a single-file export embeds supported code, data, and images in one HTML file. Neither format reconnects to live SQL or API data after export.

Exported Gantt tiles retain resource view, level collapse/expand, visible-column selection, timeline navigation and zoom, schedule health, the read-only task inspector, and the information popup. If the Gantt toolbar is saved as hidden, it also starts hidden in the exported report.

Every exported row remains available to the recipient, including rows hidden by filters. Filters are not row-level security.

docs.title: Static exports and Office
docs.text:
• Export PDF creates one static PDF page for each Qanvas page.
  • Export PowerPoint creates a slide deck with one high-resolution image per page without requiring the PowerPoint add-in.
  • The PowerPoint add-in can instead import linked or embedded Qanvas pages and tiles that can be refreshed later.

See Layout, appearance, and export and Webpage exports for the complete settings.

docs.title: Tiles and visual types
docs.text: Qanvas pages are assembled from tiles. Every tile can be positioned, resized, layered, duplicated, copied and pasted, and formatted from the Properties pane. Data-bound tiles select one document source; presentation tiles can remain independent of data.

docs.title: Data tiles
docs.text:
Tile Use it for Main design surface Table Detailed records, selected fields, sorting, totals, and conditional formatting Table designer List Editable operational rows, task lists, choices, lookups, and dates List designer Matrix Grouped rows, hierarchies, subtotals, expand/collapse, and measures Matrix designer Chart Visual comparisons, trends, distributions, and KPI plots Chart designer Gantt Tasks, dates, groups, owners, progress, milestones, and dependencies Gantt designer Card One prominent value, caption, target, comparison, or delta Card properties Multi-card A reusable card layout repeated by a dimension, with multiple fields/measures per card Multi-card designer Report Grid Manually arranged statements, formulas, measures, ranges, and formatting In-tile grid editor

Designer windows place compact property-group shortcuts above their previews. Use these shortcuts to open and focus the corresponding settings section without searching or scrolling through the full options pane. Preview elements that already link to a specific setting continue to work alongside the group shortcuts.

When you add a new page, Qanvas shows the nine page-layout choices directly on the empty canvas. Choose a starting layout there, or use the page menu later to change the layout. The choices cover Blank, Title + content, Two columns, Main + sidebar, Overview + details, Dashboard, Project plan, Four tiles, and List + details. Workflow layouts show recommended tile types in their empty areas, but Qanvas waits for you to click Add tile before adding any content.

Table, List, Matrix, Chart, Card, Multi-card, and Report Grid visuals can use source fields and Mini DAX measures. Gantt can use a linked source or keep an editable embedded task database. An embedded Gantt can expose its tasks as a Qanvas datasource for other visuals.

docs.title: Editable List
docs.text:
Choose Add tile > List, then start from Basic or Task. Basic creates an Item field plus managed id, line_no, created_at, and updated_at columns. Task adds title, description, status, priority, owner, due date, and completion date. The designer can add or remove optional fields and configure text, multiline, numeric, Boolean, date/date-time, choice, and lookup types.

An embedded List owns one manual-table source; rows are not copied into a second tile-only store. Expose as datasource controls whether other visuals can choose that source. A List can instead show an existing linked source, but linked rows are read-only until a write-back provider exists. Embedded rows are editable on the canvas, while Presentation editing is off by default and web exports remain read-only. Tab from the final editable cell creates the next row. Row commands support move, duplicate, delete, and task completion.

The movable, resizable List designer applies valid changes immediately. Its Data, Fields, Layout, Appearance, and Interaction shortcuts focus the matching property group, and clicking a preview heading or cell opens the corresponding field setup. Drag the field handle or use its compact move controls to change column order. Resize columns directly from the live List header; that column is stored as a fixed pixel width while untouched Auto/percent columns continue to share the remaining space. Duplicating or copying an embedded List creates an independent owned source with the same rows; linked Lists retain their source reference.

Each editable field can define a value used when a new row is created. Choice fields use their stored code, Boolean fields can default checked or unchecked, and date fields support dynamic Today or Current date and time values. The Task preset starts Status at Open and Priority at Normal. Appearance keeps column-header background and text colors separate, supports theme roles or manual colors, and can render header cells with rounded or square corners. The compact toolbar can independently show an optional list title and an optional search control; both the search caption and placeholder text are configurable. Editable controls inherit the row surface so text, choice, and date cells read as one row, while action buttons remain visually distinct. Dropdown arrows and calendar icons follow the active text color. Alternating rows are optional and can use either a canvas-theme role or a manual color. Grid/row-divider color and column-separator color are independent and can each follow a theme role or use a manual color. URL hover background is also theme-aware or manually selectable. URL fields can contain safe web or email links and internal document-page links. Use Choose… for a field default, or the arrow button/right-click menu in an editable row, to select either a web address or a Qanvas page. External links open in a new window; document links navigate inside the current report. A configured screen tip is shown as the readable link label and as its tooltip instead of exposing the stored URL. In Presentation mode, Add row and the row action buttons remain available only when Allow editing in Present mode is enabled.

docs.title: List Form: one record at a time
docs.text:
In the List designer, choose Layout > View > Form · one record when a wide row is easier to work with as a form. The Form view uses the same source and fields as the normal List; it does not create another copy of the data. This is especially useful for test-case registration, findings, tasks and other records with long descriptions.

Choose 1–6 form columns and set each column to Auto, percent or a fixed pixel width. In the preview, select a field and use its visual controls to move it, change its column, or increase and decrease its column span and row span. A long text control fills the height of its row span. Automatic controls follow the field type, including date pickers, choice lists, checkboxes, URL controls, numeric inputs and multiline text. Individual fields can be read-only when they should remain visible without allowing the user to change them.

The record navigator moves through the rows that remain after source, page and tile filters. Turn on Follow List selection to use a normal List as a record selector: clicking a row updates Form views that use the same source. A linked List or Form reuses the selected shared source instead of creating an extra empty source, so one central register can support registration and filtered views on several pages.

See the full table and matrix, Gantt, and Report Grid reference.

docs.title: Presentation tiles
docs.text:
• Text supports formatted headings, paragraphs, bullets, interactive checklists, links, editable tables, code/diagram blocks, compressed inline pictures, parameter text, and source or measure values. Its safe formatted HTML is suitable for one-off static flow diagrams, outlined boxes, arrows, and code panels; use SVG for exact scalable or data-bound geometry.
  • Picture supports URLs and embedded local images with fit, fill-width, and fill-height sizing.
  • SVG content supports reusable graphics, bound text and values, and either theme-derived or explicit colors. Custom geometry uses the Manual template; built-in timeline, callout, and arrow-label templates remain preferable when they already match the requested visual.

Text and Picture tiles do not require a datasource. Use them for titles, instructions, logos, illustrations, and navigation between report pages.

docs.title: Common tile behavior
docs.text:
• Select one tile or drag around several tiles to move and align them together.
  • Use handles or the Properties pane for exact size and position.
  • Use Bring to front or Send to back when tiles or graphics overlap; their submenus also contain one-step Bring forward and Send backward actions.
  • Double-click editable text to work directly on the page.
  • Press and hold an action or hyperlink control in edit mode to select its object without following the action.
  • Use source, page, and tile filters at the appropriate scope.
  • To reuse an object's appearance, right-click it and choose Copy formatting. Compatible targets on the current page receive a green dashed outline, and page tabs show how many compatible targets they contain. Click one or more outlined objects, including on other pages, then choose Done or press Escape. The painter stays active for repeated use and only accepts the same visual family: chart-to-chart, card-to-card, table-to-table, and so on. It copies theme bindings, typography, borders, fills, renderers, conditional formats and other visual-specific appearance while preserving the target's datasource, fields, measures, formulas, filter binding, text/content and actions.
  • Ctrl+C copies the selected tile or graphic. You can change pages and press Ctrl+V repeatedly to place independent copies on the destination page; copied objects retain their data bindings and complete editable setup.
  • When a long Text or Multi-card tile is active, use Up Arrow and Down Arrow to scroll its overflowing content. At the tile boundary, the same keys scroll the canvas viewport.
  • In Presentation mode, double-click a tile to focus it and return to the prior view with another double-click, Escape, or Left Arrow.

Continue with Graphics and layout or Presentation and sharing.

docs.title: Canvas tool
docs.text:
Premium/Pro feature: Canvas requires the Canvas Tool feature in the QReports license. It is available in the applicable Premium/Pro package. PowerPoint integration additionally requires the PowerPoint add-in feature.

Canvas Web creates multi-page visual reports from queries, tables, measures, parameters, charts, and formatted tiles. The current ribbon button opens the WebView report designer; the old Qanvas tool is available under Legacy tools. The same web designer is used from Excel and PowerPoint, so a visual definition follows the same query and parameter rules in both hosts.

The report structure pane is on the left, the page canvas is in the centre, and Properties and Filters are on the right. Both side panes are resizable and collapsible from their edge buttons. Select a tile to edit it; click the page background to clear the selection. Drag a tile by its header and resize it from any corner. Alignment guides appear while moving or resizing objects.

docs.title: Open Canvas
docs.text:
From Excel, choose QRep > Canvas Web. You can also right-click a supported QReports shape or picture and open its stored Canvas definition.

From PowerPoint, choose QReports > CanvasWeb to create or edit a source file, then Get from CanvasWeb to import its pages or tiles. See PowerPoint add-in.

Qanvas opens and saves standalone .qanvas files. Recent lists only valid Qanvas documents, newest first, and hides the file extension for readability. Existing .quanvas, .canvasweb.json and .qanvas.json files remain supported as legacy input formats. The embedded workbook representation remains compatible with the QReports Canvas definition used by Excel and PowerPoint.

The application theme applies to the designer, dialogs, filters, source/update/local-data workspaces, SVG editor and native loading screen. Canvas theme palettes are also available to charts and SVG graphics. Surface colors (background, text, headers, grid and controls) remain distinct from data-series palettes, so changing a chart palette does not recolor the application chrome.

The Executive indigo preset provides a dark financial-report style with deep navy/indigo surfaces, warm cream highlights, muted lavender text, and separate green/red status colors. Select it under Settings > Colors to apply the complete interface and report-color combination to new canvases. Its matching ExecutiveIndigo chart palette can also be selected independently in an existing canvas or chart.

docs.title: Select and arrange objects
docs.text:
Select one object or drag a selection rectangle around several objects. Selected objects can be moved with the mouse or arrow keys. Right-click an object to duplicate, remove, or change its layer order. The Handles command hides design handles, and Header tags hides the small Table, Matrix, Chart, or Text type labels without hiding the tile title.

Text tiles and text graphics support formatted HTML content. Double-click their content to edit directly on the canvas; double-click a tile header to edit its title. Only one text editor is active at a time. The Properties pane shows a preview and offers Edit on canvas or Edit here when the side editor is more convenient.

For a one-off, mostly static advanced composition, a Text tile is often the quickest option. Its safe formatted HTML can represent outlined callouts, boxes with arrows, code panels, and simple flow diagrams while remaining portable with the report. Prefer the SVG designer when exact scalable geometry or data-bound shapes matter, canvas shapes and connectors when each part must remain independently movable, and Multi-card when the same data-driven layout repeats for many records.

The compact text toolbar applies font, size, color, bold, italic, underline, alignment, indentation and list formatting to the selection or current caret position. With no active selection, its values become the typing format; use the whole-text action when the intention is to restyle the complete object. Paragraph styles include Normal, Heading 1, Heading 2 and Quote. Less-common insertion commands are under More so the toolbar remains usable on narrow tiles.

Use More > Insert > Date countdown for a deadline or milestone that should update automatically without a measure. Select the target date and provide configurable text for Before the date, On the date, and After the date. {days} is replaced by the absolute day difference and {date} by the formatted target date. The dialog inserts a subtle wrapping code chip such as datecountdown("2026-10-11", "Neste om {days}", "I dag", "Ferdig"), making the complete function easy to edit, copy, and paste into another text object. Normal canvas rendering, Present mode, and webpage exports display only its recalculated result.

docs.title: Pages, data sources, and parameters
docs.text:
Pages define layout, size, background, tiles, and graphics. Data sources are document-level, so the same loaded source can be reused on several pages. Every report has one protected Main source, normally created from the Excel source that opened Canvas. Add any number of Global sources when visuals need other connections or queries.

Each source owns its query and measures. Every data-bound tile initially uses Main source, but its source can be changed independently—for example, several tiles can share Global source 1 while other tiles continue to use Main source.

Use Edit query to open Query Web, Measures to manage Mini DAX measures, and Update to load or refresh the selected source. The available fields and measures follow the source of the selected tile.

Use Links… under Data sources, or right-click a source and choose Source relationships…, to match two sources by one or more keys. Choose Dimension (many → one) when a compact master table supplies descriptive fields to a larger fact source, or Measure lookup when only prepared measures are needed from the related source. For example, link a detailed P&L source to a Company master by CompanyId, and separately to a compact working-capital source by Company + Period.

Dimension fields can be used as table groups, matrix row/column axes, and chart category/group fields. Linked measures can be used as table or matrix values and as chart values/series, including in the full Chart Designer. A Company Group stored once in a 50-row master table can therefore organize visuals driven by a 50,000-row accounting source without repeating the text on every accounting row. Linked items are labelled with their source in each designer. Existing denormalized and single-source canvases continue to work without relationships or changes.

Relationships are indexed lookups, not physical row joins. Qanvas builds a shared relationship index for the loaded sources and materializes only linked fields used by a visual. The relationship editor checks the loaded rows and reports 1 : 1, 1 : many, or many : 1; a detected many-to-many relationship or non-unique Dimension key cannot be saved. A table lookup field displays (multiple) if the current row still resolves to more than one distinct value. Active source and page filters on a Dimension source propagate to every directly linked fact source using the saved dimension → fact direction. The same relationship metadata and filter propagation are included in folder and single-file webpage exports. Tile-local filters remain local to their tile.

Right-click the protected Main source and choose Reset Main source when a design no longer needs the workbook/query data that originally opened it. This clears Main source data, measures and query details while keeping the required Main source entry and the visual design. Review dependent visuals after resetting because their former fields are no longer available.

Parameters are global definitions shared by every source. A value such as period 202605 or region Europe can therefore be resolved consistently in Main source and all global sources. Excel _control values remain authoritative when Canvas is opened from a workbook.

Add source can also create an Embedded manual table or attach/create a Manual local table. Embedded tables store their JSONL rows only in the current .qanvas file. Manual local tables live on the current computer and can be reused by several reports. They share the same editor: type directly in cells, add rows, resize or reorder columns, configure types and lookups, and press Tab in the last field to create the next row. A lookup can use values from another source or turn a cell into the shared calendar picker, with optional time and ISO week numbers. Use Edit columns when schema, lookup, or delete controls are needed. The storage command converts an embedded table to a reusable local file, or takes a snapshot of a local table back into the report. View data opens cached source, embedded Gantt, and manual-table rows immediately, with search, copy, CSV export, and the appropriate Edit action.

docs.title: Tile types
docs.text:
Tile Typical use Table Detailed rows with selected columns, headers, totals, and formatting. Matrix Grouped and hierarchical data with measures, totals, and conditional formatting. Chart Visual analysis using the shared QReports chart designer. Gantt Editable tasks positioned by start/end dates, with progress, milestones, and dependencies. Card A prominent KPI value with caption, comparison, or delta. Multi-card One reusable card layout repeated for every unique value of a dimension. Text Titles, explanations, dynamic parameter text, and annotations. Picture Logos, icons, illustrations, SVG templates and other image content.

Table, Matrix, Chart, Card, and Multi-card tiles use their selected source. Text and Picture tiles are presentation objects and do not require a data field.

SVG templates can bind text and values and either inherit theme colors or use explicit overrides. The SVG editor uses the same themed form controls as the formatted-text dialog, and theme-derived SVG colors update with the selected Canvas theme.

docs.title: Create a first Canvas report
docs.text:
1. Open Canvas and add or rename the first page.
  2. Configure Main source, or add a global source, and use Edit query to retrieve data.
  3. Update the source and confirm that its fields appear under Data.
  4. Add a Table tile and select the fields to display.
  5. Add a Chart or Card using the same page data.
  6. Resize and align the tiles on the canvas.
  7. Add global parameters or source/tile filters when the report needs interaction.
  8. Hide handles and header tags to review the finished layout.
  9. Save or return the Canvas to its host.

docs.title: Tables and matrices
docs.text:
Select a table or matrix and choose Design to open the web visual builder. Its layout is consistent for both visuals: available Fields on the left, selected objects and formatting in the middle, and the live preview on the right. Drag fields into the chosen columns, rows, or values and use Advanced ordering for multi-column ascending/descending order.

Matrix rows form an ordered hierarchy. Tabular layout keeps a separate column for each row level, while Outline uses one indented hierarchy column. Parent levels can show formatted subtotals at the top or bottom, optional blank lines, and expandable +/- controls. When bottom subtotals are used, Subtotal only is the default: the total row also acts as the group heading and expands or collapses the values above it. Choose Header + subtotal when a separate group heading is preferred. Global row and subtotal controls appear before the settings for an individual row level. The lowest row level remains detail and follows the normal Table/Matrix formatting. Value headers follow their value-column alignment.

docs.title: Charts
docs.text:
Chart tiles use the shared Chart tool. Select categories and series, then configure labels, axes, gridlines, colors, markers, lines, and chart-specific options.

When a chart is saved back to Canvas, both its visible rendering and JSON definition are stored. Reopening Design Chart should restore the editor from that definition.

docs.title: Gantt schedules
docs.text:
Add a Gantt tile and open Design to map Task, Start, and End. Optional fields include Task ID, Group, Owner, Progress, Planned hours, Hours used, Status, Priority, Description, Milestone, and Depends on. Dependencies refer to Task IDs; multiple predecessors can be separated by comma, semicolon, or |.

Choose Embedded for a self-contained, editable project plan stored in the Canvas file. Choose Linked/source to map an existing source as a read-only Gantt view. Embedded plans can also display their rows as a table; linked plans can switch between table and Gantt views without writing changes back to SQL, Excel, or an API.

The frozen task table and SVG timeline use the canvas theme. Edit task names, dates, owner, status and progress directly in the table, or use the handles at the start, middle, and end of a bar to change its start, move it, or change its duration. The opposite edge remains fixed during a start/end resize, and the drag tooltip shows the effective date. Date changes update embedded rows saved in the canvas.

Use Columns to select and order visible fields. Click a column heading to sort; when grouping is enabled, projects/groups remain together and tasks are sorted within each group. Drag a header edge to resize a column. Right-click a heading to filter values, remove the active filter, hide the column, or choose date grouping/range options. Gantt-local filters are applied in addition to normal datasource filters.

The timeline supports Day, Week, Month, Quarter, and Automatic scales. Week headers show both week number and date throughout the complete range; Quarter provides a compact multi-year historical view. The same labels and scale choices are retained in webpage exports.

Projects/groups can be collapsed from their +/- control. The toolbar and task/bar context menus provide Add, Duplicate, Delete, Milestone, Owner, Status, Progress and Depends on actions. Reusable Group/Project, Owner and Status lists can define dropdown values, badges and theme/manual colors; status may also color the Gantt bar. Progress can use a badge or a multi-level progress bar.

The compact project toolbar keeps navigation and view controls together: move to the previous or next task, reveal Today or the selected task, zoom the timeline, fit the complete schedule, open schedule health, choose columns, and change grouping from More. Selecting a table row or task shape can open the compact task inspector at the bottom; turn off Show inspector when bar clicks should only select tasks. Drag the inspector's upper edge to choose how much height it uses; the height is saved with the Gantt. At normal tile widths, every control fits into three dense rows: task, status, milestone and the read-only Task ID; dates, project/group, owner, priority and progress; then hours, predecessors, notes and row actions. Narrow inspectors wrap these groups responsively instead of clipping them. Inspector controls, task menus, dropdowns and date fields use the Gantt theme. Predecessors opens a movable editor so the schedule can remain visible while dependencies are reviewed.

Dependencies stay collapsed behind Predecessors until they are needed. Its count shows whether links exist, and opening it provides the full multi-predecessor editor: search the task list, select each predecessor, or remove a selected dependency from its chip. The saved Depends on field remains compatible with linked tables by storing the task IDs as a comma-separated value. Dragging another dependency arrow adds that predecessor instead of replacing existing links.

Schedule health checks the source rows as well as the visible timeline. It reports missing task names, invalid or reversed dates, duplicate task IDs, missing predecessors, cycles, and tasks that begin before their predecessor finishes. Choose an issue to select and reveal the affected task when it is available on the timeline.

Dependencies connect task IDs. Selecting a bar or dependency can highlight the selected task and its parent/child path when Highlight connecting arrows is enabled. Missing dependency IDs, self-dependencies, circular paths, invalid dates, and an end date before the start date should be corrected before distribution. The timeline context menu controls scale, row height, table width, today line and weekend shading.

Text after each shape can show Task by default plus optional Owner, Status or Progress fields. Its typography, dependency arrows, timeline, table header, group rows, task rows, tile surface and progress/bar colors have separate theme/manual formatting areas. Click a rendered area in the designer to jump to the matching format section.

Task descriptions use the same formatted rich-text editor as text tiles and text graphics. The information button beside a bar opens a movable, resizable description editor; its Insert menu contains Link, Image, Table, Parameter, Measure, and Field. Links can open a webpage or another Qanvas page. Tables remain editable, and inserted pictures use the shared compression, resizing and alignment workflow. Use Checklist, or type -- followed by Space, to start a clickable checklist. Enter continues the checklist and Tab / Shift+Tab changes its nesting level. A collapsed caret converts only its current line to a bullet or checkbox; select several lines only when they should all become list items. The description header and task-table preview show completed / total items, such as 3/7; this count is independent of Progress. In Present mode, changes can be saved only when Allow editing in Present mode is enabled.

Editing is enabled in the normal canvas by default. Allow editing in Present mode is a separate Gantt option and is off by default so a presentation remains read-only unless explicitly enabled.

In Presentation and exported webpages, Gantt keeps its resource view, group collapse levels, column chooser, and read-only information dialog. The Gantt toolbar starts hidden when that option is selected and can be revealed without changing the saved report layout.

For an embedded schedule, enable Expose embedded tasks as a datasource to make its task rows available to cards, tables, matrices, charts, page filters, Presentation mode, and webpage exports. The published source uses the stable ID gantt:<tile-id> and points to the tile-owned task rows; the canvas file stores only a lightweight source descriptor instead of a second copy of the data. Gantt column filters remain local to the Gantt view, while filters added to the published datasource use the normal Canvas source/page/tile filter pipeline. A Gantt cannot consume its own published source. Stopping publication or deleting the source Gantt warns when dependent visuals will be moved back to the Main source.

docs.title: Parameters and filters
docs.text:
Canvas uses the shared parameter model: text, lists, hierarchical multi-select trees, date pickers, numeric inputs, formatting, and text parsing.

  • In Excel-hosted Canvas, parameters are refreshed from the workbook _control sheet.
  • In PowerPoint, parameters are stored with the presentation and can refresh all Canvas shapes.
  • Source filters apply to already loaded source data and affect every tile connected to that source.
  • Tile filters apply only to their referenced tile and remain listed with the tile name.
  • Relative-date presets such as Last 7 days apply immediately when selected; changing the accompanying day, month, or year count refreshes the same filter.

Use the same {{parameter}} syntax in SQL, Mini SQL, text, and supported visual definitions.

docs.title: Graphics and connectors
docs.text:
Canvas graphics include formatted text, action tiles, lines, rectangles, and connectors. Action tiles can open another page, refresh sources, or open parameters; their action also runs when clicked in edit mode, while right-click continues to open their design menu. To select a linked action without following it, press and hold the control. Formatted text and text tiles share headings, font styling, bullets, checklists, tables, code/diagram blocks, links, compressed inline pictures, and the Insert menu for Link, Image, Table, Date countdown, Parameter, Measure, and Field. Type - followed by Space for a bullet, or -- followed by Space for a checkbox; existing text on that line is retained. New text boxes clip cleanly at their edge by default; choose Scroll inside box for longer page-like content. Lines and rectangles support color, thickness, solid/dotted/dashed styles, shading, transparent fill, rounding, movement, and resizing. Connectors attach to defined points on tile edges and follow tiles as they move. Their route, endpoints, arrow size, line style, and layer order can be configured. Layer commands use compact Bring to front and Send to back menus; open the submenu for a one-step forward or backward move.

Canvas resize handles are shown only on selected objects. Type - followed by Space on the active line to start an automatic bullet, or -- followed by Space to start a checkbox list. Pasted HTML and plain text preserve their existing list structure and are not passed through the automatic typing shortcut. Page and linked tile filters can be placed on the canvas as button groups, cards, or multi-cards; see Visual filters on canvas.

docs.title: Report Grid
docs.text:
The Report Grid provides a spreadsheet-like layout for compact statements, KPI blocks and manually arranged report pages. A new grid starts with two rows and four blank columns. Every position is a normal A1 cell; there are no dedicated first-row column headers or first-column row labels. Cells support direct values, formulas, source fields/measures, ranges, keyboard editing, cut/paste and filters. Text is single-line by default so content cannot unexpectedly increase a row's height; Wrap text can be enabled per cell or selection. Cell formatting also supports top, middle (default), or bottom vertical alignment. Row and column filters are attached through the numbered and lettered axes.

Press F2 on any single cell to edit its current content. A measure-backed cell shows a readable measure expression in the cell and formula bar instead of only its calculated result; press Enter to commit or Escape to restore the original binding. While a formula is being edited, its colored cell/range references can be dragged to a new location. Relative references move with the selection and $ absolute row or column markers remain fixed.

Ctrl+C or Copy all copies both cell content and formatting; right-click the destination to choose Paste all, Paste formulas / values, or Paste formats. Ctrl+V continues to paste everything. The compact right-click menu groups Copy, Paste, Insert row, Insert column and Move commands into submenus; clicking a Copy/Paste/Insert parent also runs its displayed default action. Repeat last action (F4) is shown in the same menu. F4 repeats the last cell or range action on the current selection, including theme or manual formatting, number formats, alignment, borders, conditional formatting, dimensions, clearing, field/measure selection, formulas, and supported row/column operations; repeated formulas adjust relative references for each destination. While editing a formula, F4 retains its spreadsheet convention of cycling relative and absolute references. Top and bottom spacing can be reduced for layouts that need the grid close to surrounding content.

docs.title: Layout, appearance, and export
docs.text:
Canvas supports preset or manual page sizes, including widescreen/presentation and A4 portrait layouts, plus Web page · fixed width / automatic height for long scrolling reports. In web-page mode, the chosen width stays fixed while the page grows downwards to include the lowest tile or graphic. Pages also support solid colors, background images, rounded tiles, transparent Card backgrounds, optional tile borders, and explicit layer ordering. Card tiles provide configurable value and caption templates, independent typography and alignment, captions below/left/right, comparisons, conditional arrows/icons and parameter tokens. Preset or custom positive/negative/zero number formats such as +0.0;-0.0;0.0 can retain an explicit plus sign. Multi-card tiles repeat one compact card by a selected dimension and arrange field or measure values in a configurable grid. Open the Multi-card designer from Properties, F2, or the tile's right-click menu to choose the grouping field, aggregation and formatting for each value, fixed or responsive card columns, captions, text templates, borders, spacing and theme ownership. Heading, supporting text, values and value captions each have independent font, size, weight, style, alignment and color controls. Field tokens can resolve calculated text columns row by row, including date/week descriptions.

Present opens the canvas without design controls. Each page has its own Presentation resize choice: Automatic, Fit whole page, Fit width, Fit height, or Actual size (100%). Automatic fits known slide presets to the complete screen and fits manual, A4, and long web/report pages to the available width. Press F11 to enter full screen and F11 again to restore the normal window; the toolbar button provides the same toggle. Clicking a page or navigating with the arrow keys reapplies that page's configured view. The presentation toolbar provides manual zoom and fit actions. Ctrl+mouse-wheel changes this presentation zoom instead of WebView/browser zoom. Double-click a visual to smoothly enlarge and centre it; double-click it again or press Escape to return to the previous page view. Once visual focus has been restored, pressing Escape asks for confirmation before presentation mode closes, protecting the current page position and temporary annotations. Return to edit closes presentation mode directly without this confirmation. Interactive controls inside a visual do not trigger focus zoom. When space is constrained, excess page tabs move into the … menu without creating a second toolbar row. The toolbar also provides a red on-screen pointer and rectangle or oval annotations. Pointer is an independent toggle and can remain visible while either drawing tool is active. Annotations are kept separately for each page during the current presentation. Use Undo to remove the latest annotation, select the eraser icon and click a specific annotation to remove it, or use Clear page to remove all annotations from the current page. Presentation annotations are temporary and are discarded when returning to edit mode.

Application Settings includes an optional experience mode. The default mode uses the normal QReports/Qanvas wording. Qvitr mode is off by default and replaces selected labels and icons with the alternate Qvitr vocabulary and artwork. Modes are read from the experience-mode configuration so additional modes can be added later without rewriting the report format.

docs.title: AI-assisted editing
docs.text:
The Qanvas AI panel supports three workflows:

  • CLI creates or reconnects a managed workspace and sends queued requests to the configured Codex, Claude Code, or GitHub Copilot CLI provider. Qanvas verifies workspace write access before each turn, starts the CLI in that exact folder, and never enables unrestricted/bypass permission mode. Codex also receives its workspace-write policy; native Windows Claude Code has no sandbox isolation, so Qanvas uses acceptEdits, an explicit workspace-only instruction, and host-side validation.
  • External workspace creates a folder that an external ChatGPT Work task can monitor. Requests and activity are exchanged through that workspace; keep the external task active while it is processing.
  • Manual upload creates a support pack for an AI chat when no automated CLI/workspace connection is used.

Requests can include pasted screenshots and uploaded files. Attachments are copied into the AI workspace and referenced by the queued request. The conversation, request queue and live activity/status area are independently scrollable and resizable; automatic scrolling pauses when reviewing older messages.

The header AI button is a toggle: select it to open the panel, then select it again to close the panel without reaching for the panel's × button.

AI has its own top-level Settings page. It selects Codex, Claude Code, or GitHub Copilot, shows provider setup and feature-audit choices, and leaves room for future AI assistance in Query and Measures workspaces. The AI panel identifies the active engine, open report, workspace folder, and working copy. Workspace identity is stored per report, so opening or renaming a report does not silently reconnect an unrelated older workspace.

Qanvas validates the returned JSON before applying it. The exported AI guidance describes native tiles, Gantt, rich text, theme bindings, hyperlinks, embedded images and purpose-built SVGs. It explicitly checks that requested features exist in the document rather than accepting a written claim. A custom SVG created from scratch must be stored as kind: "svgGraphic" with lowercase nested svgGraphic.template: "manual"; the standalone element belongs only in nested svgGraphic.svgCode. This rule is sent to Codex, Claude, and Copilot on every turn, including resumed conversations. GitHub Copilot can run additional feature-audit/repair turns; disable Run automatic feature audit and repair turns in Settings for faster small edits while retaining the structural validation pass.

AI-generated changes should still be reviewed visually. Validation proves the document is structurally usable, not that every image, layout choice or factual statement is correct.

The header can create or open a standalone Canvas document, maintain recent files, and save changes. When hosted by Excel or PowerPoint, returning to the host captures the page and stores both the rendered image and editable definition.

docs.title: Return to Excel
docs.text:
When hosted by Excel, Return to Excel stores the Canvas specification with the workbook shape and replaces or inserts its rendered image. Loading the worksheet refreshes stored Canvas shapes through an off-screen render-only process, so the editor does not open or flash during a normal report refresh.

Keep the underlying workbook connections, _control parameters, and report code with the workbook. The rendered picture is only the visible result; the stored Canvas JSON is required for later editing.

docs.title: Use Canvas in PowerPoint
docs.text:
The PowerPoint add-in imports a selected Canvas page or tile as a picture on the slide. The picture stores a link to the source .qanvas file, the selected object, and any import filters. Edit the source file in CanvasWeb, then use Update canvases to rerender linked pictures.

PowerPoint provides CanvasWeb, Get from CanvasWeb, Update canvases, and Parameters. See the PowerPoint QRep Ribbon.

docs.title: Direct tile properties and local pictures
docs.text:
Chart properties expose the shared chart settings directly in the Canvas pane; see Chart tool. Matrix Subtotals exposes the selected-row subtotal settings, pretext, expand/collapse and initial collapse, layout, repeated tabular labels, blank lines, outline row header and subtotal position. Header columns remain fixed during horizontal scrolling. Matrix designs support up to 2,000 displayed items; large matrices still affect rendering performance. Data bars place positive and negative values on opposite sides of a common zero baseline and can apply to groups and details.

Picture tiles accept direct image URLs or Choose image local files. Local images are embedded in the saved report. Image settings includes the picker, URL, hidden scrollbars and a Wikimedia Commons reference. General settings holds sizing, background and transparency. Image sizing supports Fit to window (whole picture), Fill width and Fill height, with a minimum tile height of 30.

Card formatting, Target and variance, and Text sections are collapsible. Graphics have General settings for position/size and separate Rectangle, Line or Connector settings. Not all property sections currently use the same order: General settings may appear near Header settings; a consistent ordering review is still pending.

docs.title: Hyperlinks in text
docs.text: In the formatted text editor, place the cursor or select text and choose Link…. Choose http (default), https or no prefix; enter display text and a screen tip. Place in this document links to another Canvas page. Links are underlined by default, with a no-underline option. Put the cursor inside an existing link and choose Link to edit it. Internal page links also navigate exported report tabs. External links still require network access.

docs.title: Portable report saves
docs.text: Saving a .qanvas file packages referenced local sources and embedded pictures with the editable report, so it can be copied to a shared file area. SQL/API credentials and external infrastructure are not made portable by this save; test reopening on another computer before distribution.

docs.title: Webpage exports
docs.text:
Choose Export webpage… and create a named export definition. Settings and last successful export date are stored in the Canvas document: save the Canvas file to persist them. Save settings does not export; Export / update writes the report.

The export dialog follows the active application theme. SVG tiles are packaged with the SVG runtime in both folder and single-file exports.

  • File settings: Folder website or Single HTML file, target folder, and filename for single-file exports. The default single filename is the report name; .html is added automatically. Change the filename to keep a historic copy in the same folder. Re-exporting the same Qanvas filename replaces that export, but unrelated HTML files are protected.
  • Filters: Automatic/all columns or selected columns, filter types, and horizontal/top or vertical/left-pane layout. The filter field list is bordered and scrollable.
  • Report appearance: optional report name with size/color/bold/italic/underline; optional Subheader text on a new line with separate formatting; selected and unselected button colors. A preview shows these choices.

Folder exports include index.html, application files, exported data, images and an export marker. Choose an empty folder or an existing Qanvas export folder. Keep the whole folder together. Single HTML exports embed application code, styles, data and supported images in one file, with no sidecar files. Both formats can be opened locally in a modern browser. Hosted access requires a suitable web server; uploading HTML to a SharePoint document library is file distribution, not normal static hosting.

Pages become tabs; exported tables/matrices support header sorting and matrix expansion. Filters use only exported, already loaded rows, with no live SQL/API refresh. Filter types are Basic, Advanced (comparisons/contains/from-to), Multiple values (All/Clear), Date, Date range, Buttons and Toggle (on/off plus All values). Date controls use an Apply/Cancel/Clear calendar, highlight today, and adapt to narrow screens. Choose date(s) uses selected colors; date boxes use unselected colors.

Security: every exported row is accessible to recipients, including rows hidden by filters. Filters are not row-level access control. Protect the entire hosting package, not just the landing page. Browser-download rules, large datasets and embedded images can affect size and performance. Re-export to update existing offline reports.

docs.title: Current considerations
docs.text:
• Test queries in Query Tool before building a large visual page.
  • Large images and many detailed tiles increase rendering time and file size.
  • Keep connection credentials out of Canvas text and screenshots.
  • API-backed page-query behavior can vary by version; API Explorer and Query Tool remain the supported definition path.
  • A rendered image without its stored Canvas definition cannot be reopened for full editing.

Continue with Query Tool, Parameters, Chart tool, or PowerPoint add-in.

docs.title: Export all pages as PDF
docs.text:
Export PDF saves every canvas page as a separate page in one static PDF, in report tab order. Choose a filename in the save dialog. It uses the existing Microsoft WebView2 runtime, with no additional PDF installation. The PDF uses the largest canvas dimensions as its paper size; smaller canvases are fitted proportionally. It preserves the canvas background. Designer panes and resize handles are omitted.

Export uses the current filter state and returns you to your original report tab. PDF does not retain interactive filters, scrolling or matrix expansion; scrollable tiles show their current viewport. Use webpage export when readers need interactive results.

docs.title: Export all pages to PowerPoint
docs.text:
Choose Export > Export PowerPoint… to create a .pptx with one slide per Canvas page, in page order. Each slide contains a high-resolution image of its page. Pages with a different aspect ratio from the first page are fitted and centered on the slide. The export uses the current loaded data and filter state, then returns to the page you were editing.

The slides are static pictures. To change their data or design, update the Canvas and export again. This export runs in QanvasWeb without the PowerPoint add-in or a separate PowerPoint installation; PowerPoint or another compatible viewer is needed to open the resulting file.

docs.title: Visuelle filtre på canvas
docs.text: Første fungerende versjon er implementert. Den støtter page filters og linked tile filters i editor, presentasjon og web-eksport. Source filters er med hensikt ikke valgbare.

docs.title: Mål
docs.text:
En eksisterende side- eller tile-filterdefinisjon skal kunne vises som knapper, en enkel dropdown, kort eller et multi-card direkte på canvas. Et valg oppdaterer den samme filterdefinisjonen som filterpanelet bruker. Funksjonen er derfor en ny visning av dagens filter, ikke et nytt filtersystem.

Første versjon bør støtte page filter og tile filter. Source filter holdes utenfor fordi et visuelt filter på én side ellers kan endre datagrunnlaget på andre sider uten at brukeren ser hvor endringen kommer fra.

docs.title: Brukerflyt
docs.text:
1. Brukeren oppretter filteret i filterpanelet som i dag.
  2. Velg Add visual… på filteret.
  3. Brukeren velger visning:
  4. Button group
  5. Dropdown
  6. Cards
  7. Multi-card
  8. Visualen plasseres på gjeldende side og er koblet til filteret.
  9. Klikk på et element setter eller fjerner filterverdien og bruker dagens filterpipeline til å tegne berørte visuals på nytt.
  10. Filteret kan fortsatt redigeres i filterpanelet. Endringer vises automatisk i den koblede visualen.

Visualen kan også opprettes fra Graphics > Visual filter. Designeren velger et eksisterende page/tile-filter. Hvis siden ikke har et slikt filter, opprettes et ordinært page-filter med første tilgjengelige kolonne som startpunkt.

docs.title: Datamodell
docs.text:
Alle page- og tile-filterdefinisjoner får en stabil id. Canvas-visualen lagrer bare en lett referanse, for eksempel:

{
  "kind": "visualFilter",
  "visualFilter": {
    "filterRef": {
      "scope": "page",
      "filterId": "filter-123"
    },
    "layout": "cards",
    "heading": "{{field:category}}",
    "supportingText": "{{measure:item_count}}",
    "imageField": "image_url",
    "columns": 3,
    "showAll": true
  }
}

For tile-scope peker filterId på den eksisterende delte tile-filterdefinisjonen (sharedFilterId) og beholder dagens target-liste. Visualen skal aldri kopiere filterverdien til en egen lokal tilstand; valgt verdi leses fra og skrives til filterobjektet.

docs.title: Button group
docs.text:
• Én knapp per unik dimensjonsverdi.
  • Enkeltvalg eller flervalg følger filtertypen.
  • Valgfri All / Clear-knapp. All kan vise de samme radtellingene, feltene og measures som de øvrige valgene, aggregert over alle tilgjengelige rader.
  • Støtter tekst, bilde, flere value-felt og valgt/ikke-valgt formatering.
  • Knappene fordeler tilgjengelig bredde og høyde i visualen. Når visualen skaleres, skaleres derfor også knappene i stedet for å beholde en fast innholdsbredde.

docs.title: Dropdown
docs.text:
• Kompakt dropdown for filterfelt. Lange verdilister har søk øverst uten en permanent scrollbar ved siden av den lukkede kontrollen.
  • Bruker den samme page/tile-filtertilstanden som de øvrige layoutene.
  • All / Clear vises som første valg når den er aktivert. Uten All/Clear vises en nøytral tomtilstand frem til brukeren velger en verdi.

docs.title: Cards og multi-card
docs.text:
• Én card per unik verdi i filterets dimensjon.
  • Kan vise heading, supporting text, bilde og flere aggregerte felt/measures.
  • Multi-card-layoutet har et eget value-grid med 1–6 kolonner. Hvert value-felt kan bruke automatisk plassering, festes til en bestemt kolonne eller spenne over flere rader/full kolonne. Kolonnene kan bruke automatisk, prosentvis eller fast pikselbredde, på samme måte som den ordinære Multi-card-flisen.
  • Hvert value-felt kan bruke Number, Image, Badge, Icon eller DataBar samt databar/bullet graph og conditional formatting. Formateringen kan styres av et annet felt eller measure enn verdien som vises.
  • Heading og supporting text støtter {{value}}, {{count}}, {{field:name}} og {{measure:name|aggregation}}.
  • Hele cardet er klikkbart og viser tydelig valgt tilstand.

Verdilisten beregnes fra filterets datasource etter andre aktive filtre. Filteret som visualen selv styrer må midlertidig utelates når tilgjengelige valg beregnes, ellers forsvinner ikke-valgte alternativer etter første klikk. Avhengige filtre følger dagens dependency-logikk.

docs.title: Interaksjon
docs.text:
• Presentasjon og web-eksport: vanlig klikk filtrerer.
  • Edit mode: klikk på knapp/card filtrerer; klikk på tomt område eller ramme velger visualen for flytting og skalering. Høyreklikk åpner designer.
  • Ctrl/Cmd kan følge dagens multi-select-regler der filtertypen støtter flere verdier.
  • Escape endrer ikke filteret. En eksplisitt Clear/All-handling nullstiller det.
  • Tastatur: Tab til valg, Space/Enter velger, aria-pressed/aria-selected viser tilstand.

docs.title: Designer
docs.text:
Designeren er flyttbar og kan endre størrelse. Den velger eksisterende page/tile-filter og dimensjon, samt layout, sortering, innhold, value-liste, bilde og utseende. Preview bruker den virkelige filtertilstanden. Høyreklikk på visualen og velg Edit in designer for å åpne den igjen. Høyreklikk i heading, supporting text eller en value-caption åpner innsetting av tekstfunksjon, felt, measure eller parameter. Enter i et vanlig editorfelt lagrer feltendringen uten å lukke dialogen. Klikk på heading, supporting text, value eller caption i preview for å hoppe til den tilhørende innstillingen. Snarveiene over preview åpner og fokuserer Layout, Card content, Values og Appearance.

Foreslåtte innstillinger:

  • Filter binding: page eller linked tile filter.
  • Layout: buttons, dropdown, cards, multi-card.
  • Dimensjon/verdi, sortering og maksimal antall valg.
  • Heading, supporting text, values/measures, bilde eller ikon.
  • Maksimalt antall kolonner, gap, padding, bakgrunn, kant og avrunding. Hvis visualen har færre valg enn maksimum, fordeles de over hele tilgjengelig bredde i stedet for å reservere tomme kolonner.
  • Selected, unselected, hover og disabled appearance. Valgt tilstand kan vises med bakgrunnsfarge, kun en kant som ellers er usynlig, eller både bakgrunn og kant. Kantbredden kan konfigureres.
  • Valgbare temaroller for tekst, bakgrunn og kant, separat for valgt og ikke valgt tilstand. Egne farger kan fortsatt brukes når canvas-tema er slått av.
  • Show All/Clear, single/multiple selection og tom-verdi-label.
  • Optional conditional-formatting source, også fra et annet measure.

docs.title: Avgrensning og anbefalt løsning
docs.text:
Løsningen bruker stabile filter-ID-er og én felles funksjon for å oppdatere et filter fra både filterpanelet og visualen. Valgt verdi lagres aldri i visualen. Når valglisten beregnes, brukes source-, page- og tile-filterpipeline som før, men visualens eget filter utelates slik at ikke-valgte alternativer ikke forsvinner.

Levert i første versjon:

  1. Stabile ID-er på page/tile filters og felles oppdateringsfunksjon.
  2. Button group, Dropdown, Cards og Multi-card-layout.
  3. Page filters og linked tile filters med eksisterende target-liste.
  4. Valgbare temaroller eller egne selected/unselected-farger, kolonner, gap, padding og avrunding.
