  5. Heading, supporting text, bilde og aggregert felt/measure.
  6. Presentasjonsmodus, web-eksport, tastaturknapper og aria-pressed.
  7. Tester for page-filter, linked tile-filter, designer, bevarte valg og web-eksport.
  8. Responsive knapper og minimumshøyde på 30 piksler for kompakte filterfelt.
  9. Søk i lange dropdown-lister, kompakt datovelger og synkron valgt-markering mellom flere visualer som peker til samme filter.
  10. Felt og measures fra direkte relaterte kilder når den lagrede datasource-relasjonen gjør bindingen gyldig.

Aktuelle utvidelser er ikonvelger og flere dropdown-varianter. Datamodellen er lagt slik at disse kan bygges videre uten et nytt filtersystem.

Source filters kan vurderes senere, men bør da kreve en eksplisitt advarsel og en tydelig global indikator på alle sider.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
User-visible changes are grouped by calendar week. Dates identify the Monday-to-Sunday period in which the work was completed.

WEEK44

26 October–1 November 2026

List forms and smoother shared registration
  • Added List Form, a new List view that shows and edits one record at a time. It is useful for test cases, tasks, findings and other registrations with many fields.
  • Made forms easy to arrange visually. Choose the number and width of columns, move fields in the preview, and let a field span several columns or rows. Long text, dates, choices, checkboxes, numbers, sliders and links use controls suited to their field type.
  • Added compact field settings, read-only fields, default values and a selected-row highlight. A normal List can act as the selector while a Form view shows the selected record from the same source.
  • Improved shared Lists so a linked List reuses the existing embedded source instead of creating an extra empty source. Lists and forms can therefore share one central register across pages.
  • Fixed List filters and record selection in Presentation mode so they follow the same values and single-selection rules as Edit mode.
  • Polished List and Form layout: headers and values align correctly, alternating row bands fill the full width, one-row and multi-row text boxes keep readable labels, and URL fields show their friendly screen tip instead of the stored address.
  • New pages now show nine distinct page layouts, including Overview + details, Dashboard, Project plan, Four tiles, and List + details. Layouts wait for you to choose when to add content.
  • Fixed the installer header so dialog titles and explanations no longer overlap the Qvitr branding.
  • Improved Matrix subtotals. Bottom subtotals now use one clean total row by default, with the expand or collapse button on that row instead of repeating the group heading. The previous two-row style is still available, and the related settings are arranged in a clearer order.
WEEK43

19–25 October 2026

Reusable report content, richer editing and faster source workflows
  • Added Qanvas-to-Qanvas import for complete editable pages, page and tile filters, related sources and selected measures. Sources can also be imported without pages, with footprint matching and explicit choices to reuse, replace, skip or create a separate source when definitions collide.
  • Added editable manual tables stored either inside a Qanvas file or as reusable local files. The grid supports row and column editing, column types, lookup values from other sources, a calendar lookup with optional time and ISO week numbers, column resizing/reordering, automatic row creation with Tab, and conversion between embedded and file storage.
  • Added a dedicated editable List tile on top of the embedded manual-table model. New Lists offer Basic and Task presets with stable IDs, automatic line numbers and created/updated timestamps; typed custom fields, code/label choices, source lookups, and safe external/document-page URL fields; search, sorting, row move/duplicate/delete/complete actions; theme roles; and a live movable/resizable designer. Fields can be reordered by drag or compact move controls, columns can be resized directly, and new-row defaults support choices, booleans, Today and current date/time. Embedded Lists can be exposed as ordinary datasources, copied with independent owned data, and optionally edited in Presentation mode, while linked sources and web exports remain read-only.
  • Expanded List appearance and interaction controls with optional title/search text, left/right search alignment, separate header, row, grid-line and column-separator colors, square or rounded headers, alternating rows, theme-aware URL hover surfaces, and calendar/dropdown controls that inherit row text and surface colors. URL screen tips now act as the readable link label and tooltip, internal page links navigate correctly, and Add row plus row action controls work in Presentation mode when editing is enabled.
  • Added an instant in-Qanvas source-data viewer and consolidated source actions for viewing data, editing queries or measures, links, rename and delete without reloading an already cached preview.
  • Expanded Report Grid copy, paste and repeat behavior. Cell aggregation, fields and measures now copy with the cell; one copied cell can fill a multi-cell selection; and F4 repeats formatting, number formats, alignment, borders, dimensions, formulas, field/measure selections and row/column operations on a new selection. The right-click menu now groups Copy, Paste, Insert and Move commands into compact submenus while keeping their most common parent actions directly clickable. Locale-formatted numeric selections calculate correctly, and empty filtered values behave as zero in arithmetic.
  • Improved Report Grid formula editing: F2 now enters edit mode for values, formulas, fields and measure-backed cells, showing a readable measure expression in the cell and formula bar; Enter commits and Escape restores the original binding. Colored formula references can be dragged to another range while preserving relative and absolute-reference semantics.
  • Refined Report Grid sizing and selection with continuous explicit row heights, clipped single-line content by default, opt-in wrapping, vertical alignment, clearer row numbers around filter badges, and improved row/column filter editing.
  • Improved formatted text with reliable pasted tables, code blocks and whitespace-sensitive diagrams, an Insert table command, scroll-inside-box overflow, and inline images with alignment, proportional resizing and the same compression workflow as image tiles. A new readable datecountdown("date","future","today","past") function inserts configurable future, today and completed text that recalculates automatically without a measure and remains easy to edit, copy, and paste.
  • Improved Gantt task descriptions with page and external links, interactive checklists, preserved text when - or -- is converted to a list item, and visible navigation when an internal page link is followed. Task priorities support Low, Normal and High with configurable icons and theme-aware colors.
  • Added default Open, In progress and Completed Gantt statuses while retaining editable labels, and made embedded or local manual Gantt sources available through the normal table viewer.
  • Reworked the Gantt task inspector into a compact, saved-height bottom panel. Task and milestone, schedule/assignment, and status/progress/hours now use three dense rows; Task ID is a read-only reference and the multi-predecessor editor stays collapsed until requested. The inspector can be disabled for bar clicks, its spacing has been tightened further, and its surfaces, inputs, dropdowns, date controls and actions now follow the active Gantt theme. The predecessor editor is a normal button that opens a movable inspection dialog.
  • Added a simplified Gantt project toolbar, schedule-health panel, zoom/navigation controls and dependency editor. The task context menu now follows the Gantt theme, and appearance controls that do not apply to the selected input style are disabled instead of implying that they will affect it.
  • Improved charts with consistent tile/designer plot spacing, full-size treemap rendering, aligned value axes for multiples, reorganized doughnut controls with independent center/category typography, line breaks and safer ring-label placement, configurable rounded ends for bar and column charts, and an optional background-colored gap around line/scatter markers. Label spacing can always retain the first and/or last value, and markers can be limited to points that still have a visible label. Clicking a line or marker now opens Line & markers instead of Data labels; the Properties pane also exposes editable chart titles and the most-used line, marker and bar-layout controls.
  • Fixed direct chart-property refresh so Use canvas theme, background and gridline changes redraw immediately without reopening and reapplying the designer. Changing a line chart to a bar chart now preserves a visible plot, and duplicated charts retain independent, editable top positions instead of being constrained by stale geometry.
  • Added an Executive indigo report theme inspired by dark financial dashboards, with deep navy surfaces, warm cream accents, lavender text, green/red status roles and a matching eight-color chart palette.
  • Reorganized tile and graphic property groups, removed duplicate Content sections, kept Properties/Filters tabs visible while scrolling, and improved narrow-pane layouts and source action labels.
  • Added compact property-group shortcuts above the preview in Chart, Table, Matrix, Gantt and SVG designers, matching the existing Visual filter and Multi-card navigation. The shortcuts open collapsed groups, scroll to them and place keyboard focus on the selected section.
  • Recent Qanvas files are now deduplicated by path, and Settings controls how many entries are retained and shown, from 1 to 25 with a default of 10.
  • AI workspaces are now connected per report instead of through one global last-used pointer. Renamed or newly opened reports no longer inherit an unrelated workspace, new workspace copies use .qanvas, and the AI panel shows the selected engine plus the full open-report, workspace and working-copy paths.
  • Moved AI configuration to its own top-level Settings page and added Claude Code, Codex and GitHub Copilot guidance for current rich text, Gantt, local-table and Manual SVG authoring. Custom generated SVG now explicitly uses nested svgGraphic.template: "manual" on every provider turn, including resumed sessions.
  • Added a dedicated SVG designer with a collapsible reusable-template gallery, custom SVG analysis, editable text/typography/links and shape colors/borders, explicit category-slot bindings, and automatic Today/fixed/field/parameter date-marker placement on detected timeline axes. Clicking the preview selects the matching component control, and duplicating a detected date marker creates another independently configurable dynamic marker. Marker placement now moves only its own label, badge and line, including in existing duplicated SVGs, without shifting a containing background shape. Its live preview uses the same tile ratio and render path as the applied graphic. Text inputs now share the searchable token lookup for source fields, linked measures, parameters and functions, and preview selection no longer lets the fixed header or Apply/Cancel footer cover designer controls.
  • Added a Multi-card tile and designer. One reusable card layout can repeat by a dimension, show configurable field or measure values in columns, aggregate raw columns with First, Sum, Average, Min, Max or Count, and inherit the canvas theme or use explicit card colors and borders. The designer is also available from the tile's right-click menu and provides independent typography for headings, supporting text, values and captions. Calculated text columns now evaluate row by row before visual aggregation, fixing date/week captions that previously displayed NaN.
  • Multi-card value rows are now compact by default, with format, alignment, placement, cell display, data bars and conditional formatting under More. Conditional formatting can use a separate field/measure, repeated cards can show a conditional edge band, and caption/template inputs offer a right-click insert menu for fields, measures, parameters and text functions.
  • Upgraded the single Card tile with the same value/caption typography, placement, alignment, comparison, conditional icon/arrow and number-format controls used by Multi-card. Custom positive/negative/zero formats can retain an explicit + sign for positive values, and positive and negative conditional arrows can be configured independently.
  • Added visual filters on the canvas. Existing page filters and linked tile filters can be shown as responsive button groups, compact dropdowns, cards or multi-cards with live selected state, selectable canvas-theme roles or custom colors, optional images and multiple aggregated values. Filter multi-cards support 1–6 value columns, automatic/fixed/percent column widths and per-value column/row-span placement. Selection can be highlighted by background, border only, or both. Values support the multi-card renderers, data bars and conditional formatting; All/Clear can show totals and measures; and text fields have a right-click token menu. The same filter object drives editor, Presentation and exported webpages, the visual keeps non-selected choices available while filtering, and compact visual-filter tiles can be resized down to 30 pixels high.
  • Improved visual-filter authoring with a movable/resizable designer, preview-to-property navigation and the common property-group shortcut strip. Column count is now a maximum so fewer choices use the full available width. Dropdowns remain selectable, avoid an unnecessary side scrollbar and provide search for long lists; the compact date-range picker now lays out days correctly. Multiple visuals bound to the same filter highlight together, and valid measures from related sources are available to card-style filter values.
  • Fixed inherited presentation filters so separate filters on the same datasource column retain their stable identities and selection modes. Visual filters using Follow filter type now remain interactive and single-select for Dropdown filters in Presentation mode instead of becoming a combined multi-selection filter.
  • Added a repeatable Copy formatting painter to the right-click menu for tiles and graphics. Compatible targets are outlined, page tabs show compatible target counts, and formatting can be applied to multiple same-family objects across pages without replacing their data bindings or content. The normal Ctrl+C/Ctrl+V object clipboard can also paste complete editable tiles and graphics onto another page and remains reusable for repeated pastes.
  • Simplified object layer commands into Bring to front and Send to back submenus, with one-step forward/backward commands still available inside them. In edit mode, holding an action or hyperlink control selects its object without following the destination, making linked controls easier to move and format.
  • Added a Measure-workspace color picker that previews and inserts theme roles or fixed hex colors, plus the field context-menu template fields_pickcolor for building a variable-based color SWITCH measure. Canvas palette swatches and the dedicated eyedropper now remain active until a report color is sampled or the operation is cancelled.
  • Up and Down Arrow now scroll the active long text or Multi-card tile before falling back to the canvas viewport, so selected overflowing content can be read without using the scrollbar.
  • Presentation mode now starts on the page currently open in the editor instead of returning to the first page, and F11 toggles full screen on or off.
  • Pressing F now shows or hides the filter panel in Presentation mode and exported webpages without changing the saved filter values.
  • Compressed the Presentation and webpage-export top bar: page tabs remain on the first row, excess pages move under …, Zoom and Annotations are easier-to-open collapsed menus, and auto-hidden controls overlay the report instead of resizing it.
  • Presentation and web-export profiles now inherit the canvas editor's source and page filters by default, including their current values and page scope. Individual source, page and tile filters can be locked so they remain active as authored report constraints without appearing as viewer controls; the previous manual export-filter setup remains available when inheritance is disabled.
  • Added complete Week labels and a Quarter scale to Gantt timelines. Exported Gantt views now retain resource view, level collapse, visible columns, read-only task information and the saved hidden-toolbar state.
  • Improved Query workspace manual-table editing and resized the date picker into a compact, responsive calendar that remains usable in narrow windows.
  • Fixed the enterprise updater's download-progress dialog and added direct release-note access before installation plus a release-note prompt the next time Qanvas opens after a successful upgrade.
  • Restyled the update checker with the active Qanvas theme and branded the enterprise install, upgrade, progress and completion dialogs with the Qvitr visual design.
  • Fixed elevated update launches so the Qvitr Enterprise installer is restored and brought in front of other application windows instead of opening unnoticed behind them.
WEEK42

12–18 October 2026

Manual enterprise updates and safer GitHub releases
  • Simplified Report Grid to one rectangular A1 cell model. The former dedicated column-header, row-label and corner cells were removed; every grid cell now supports the same content, formatting and formula behavior, while filters remain on the row and column axes.
  • Added a user-initiated Check for updates command to Qanvas, Excel and PowerPoint. Enterprise installations never check automatically.
  • Added a dedicated GitHub qvitr-update.json manifest with separate Qanvas file and MSI installer versions, setup URL, release URL and SHA-256 hash.
  • Added confirmation, download progress, hash checking, Authenticode presence checking and elevated setup launch to the shared Qanvas updater.
  • Added a one-command GitHub release script that can build, sign, stage, validate and upload Qvitr Enterprise, with validation-only, draft and reuse-existing-build options.
  • Strengthened release validation so the update manifest, MSI and bootstrapper must agree with the requested version and installer hash before upload.
  • Updated installer guidance to require a new three-part MSI version for each release; signing certificates do not require the installer version to remain fixed.
  • Added direct Qanvas source relationships with multi-field keys and explicit Dimension or Measure lookup roles. Linked dimension fields can group tables, form matrix axes, and drive chart categories/groups without physically expanding the primary detail table. Source and page filters on a Dimension master propagate to directly linked fact sources. Tables, matrices, charts, and the full Chart Designer can use measures from a linked, pre-aggregated source. The relationship editor reports loaded-data cardinality and requires a unique Dimension key.
  • Fixed folder and single-file webpage exports so source relationships remain in the offline snapshot. Exported visuals now calculate linked fields/measures and propagate filters from Dimension master tables in the same way as Presentation mode.
  • Fixed native Mini DAX source-field parsing so physical names containing underscores, including accounts_receivable, are aggregated correctly instead of being truncated at the first underscore.
  • Added measure-driven Report Grid crossfilters. Row and column filters can use {{measure:name}} to resolve a scalar from the effective cell source before filtering the displayed measure; explicit and legacy parameter tokens remain supported.
  • Corrected the MiniDAX function reference so CAST target types and DATEPART part names use quoted text, with working numeric-conversion and week-number examples in both native and web Measure workspaces.
  • Added Find unused to Measure workspace Tools. It marks measures with neither formula dependants nor references in the current Qanvas document, opens each candidate for review, and deliberately leaves deletion manual; calculated columns are excluded from the cleanup scan.
  • Canvas parameters now resolve inside MiniDAX measures during validation, matrix testing, charts, Presentation and webpage output. The Measures function reference lists parameters, and typing {{ opens parameter autocomplete.
  • Replaced free-text chart format fields with the same preset/custom format selector in both Chart Designer and the chart Properties pane.
  • Added Claude Code as a Qanvas AI CLI provider. Codex and Claude sessions are now provider-specific, Qanvas verifies workspace write access before every turn, and the built-in setup guidance distinguishes Windows folder permissions from ChatGPT Work access.
  • Report Grid cells now keep text on one clipped line by default so content cannot unexpectedly enlarge rows. Wrapping can be enabled per cell or multi-cell selection, and vertical alignment supports top, middle, or bottom with middle as the default.
WEEK41

5–11 October 2026

Editable project plans, stronger AI workflows and safer measures
  • Added the native Gantt tile with embedded editable task data or linked read-only data. It supports task IDs, projects/groups, owners, status, progress, milestones, descriptions and dependencies; an optional published Gantt datasource can drive other visuals and normal Presentation/Web filters.
  • Expanded Gantt interaction with direct table editing, sortable/resizable columns, column filters and menus, collapsible groups, bar drag handles, date tooltips, timeline options, a movable/resizable rich-description editor, pure-Gantt view, Present-mode editing and webpage interaction. Selected tasks and dependency paths can be highlighted.
  • Added interactive checklists to Gantt task descriptions, including a toolbar action, -- + Space quick entry, normal bulleted sublists, explicitly nested checklists, saved checked state, and completed / total counters in the editor, task table and interactive description preview. Description previews remain open while the pointer moves into them or checks an item, close when the pointer leaves, and hide while the full description editor is open.
  • Presentation settings now hide disabled pointer and annotation tools consistently in normal Present view, including its right-click menu and annotation shortcuts.
  • Added theme/manual formatting for Gantt table areas, groups, bars, progress, status badges, dependency arrows and labels. Project, owner and status registries provide reusable dropdown values and colors.
  • Reworked formatted text so the canvas editor is the primary editor. Selection/caret formatting now includes font, size, color, bold, italic, underline, lists and Normal/H1/H2/Quote styles, with less-common insert commands in a compact menu.
  • Expanded Qanvas AI with CLI, external-workspace and manual-support-pack flows, queued requests, file/screenshot attachments, activity messages, resizable panes and stronger host/feature validation. Copilot's slower automatic feature audit and repair turns can be disabled independently of structural validation.
  • Added native-Gantt and custom-SVG guidance to the exported AI skill, including checks that requested images, links, timelines and theme bindings really exist instead of being claimed in text.
  • Added connection-level API parameters shared by every API on a connection. Effective values now follow connection defaults → API defaults → Excel/Canvas/Query launch values, without writing temporary caller values back to saved definitions.
  • Expanded Measure workspace with reference auditing, invalid-formula checks, rename propagation into dependent measures and Canvas objects, a compact Tools menu, progress feedback, folders, a complete searchable function reference and expression helper. Date functions including TODAY() are supported by Canvas visuals.

docs.title: Chart tool
docs.text: The Chart tool opens the chart designer with the current Query Tool result. It supports chart selection, series definitions, labels, formatting, filters, and returning chart definitions to Excel or Canvas.

docs.title: Chart Web workflow
docs.text:
Choose a chart type, select Values and Category, and configure its series. Chart Web supports Bar/column, Stacked, Line, Area, Scatter, Waterfall, Histogram, Boxplot, Treemap, Heatmap, Gauge, Pie and Doughnut. Data and options panes can be resized or collapsed; chart-type settings are collapsible groups. The shortcut strip above the preview opens Data or any property group directly, including groups that are currently collapsed. The designer chrome, loading surface and preview palette follow the selected Canvas/application theme unless a chart-specific override is selected.

The built-in ExecutiveIndigo palette matches the Executive indigo canvas preset: cream primary series, subdued lavender comparison series, and green/red supporting colors on dark financial-report surfaces.

When opened from a Canvas tile, the preview uses the tile's source and local filters. The footer indicates row/series counts and global/local filter counts. Design changes are returned as an editable chart specification.

docs.title: Category, Group and Multiple
docs.text:
• Category identifies the plotted items, such as year or date.
  • Group is a logical parent level, such as week above dates. Supported plots can show shaded groups with configurable strength, separator color and thickness, including Waterfall.
  • Multiple splits data by another field, such as country. Use Show as multiples for separate panels rather than splitting series in one plot.

Multiple settings include maximum panel count, shared value/category axes, automatic or explicit rows and columns, spacing, and panel-header alignment, size, color, bold, italic and underline. Review the filters and category settings when expected categories are missing.

docs.title: Labels and axes
docs.text:
Category and value axes have visibility, text size/color, formatting and spacing controls. Category ordering supports natural, category ascending/descending and value ascending/descending. Data labels control visibility, category, value, series name, delimiter (including line breaks), placement, text size/color, format, angle and spacing. Always show first value and Always show last value preserve either endpoint when spacing hides intermediate labels; selecting only the last option anchors high spacing from the end. Group labels have separate content and typography controls.

Date formatting supports ddd (short weekday), dddd (full weekday) and ww (week). Automatic spacing reduces label crowding; it is distinct from filtering the data. Series-sensitive groups offer All or individual-series settings for data labels, line/markers and scatter/plot settings.

docs.title: Chart-specific controls
docs.text:
• Bar/column and Stacked: orientation, bar width, spacing, shading, and End rounding %. Use 0 for square ends and increase the percentage for a softer rounded cap; 50 is fully rounded.
  • Line and Area: line and marker settings. Background gap around markers paints a configurable outline in the chart background color behind each marker, visually separating it from the line without requiring a manually synchronized border color. Only show markers with visible labels hides intermediate markers suppressed by label spacing, which makes a clean last-value-only or endpoint-only line possible.
  • Scatter: plot and marker settings.
  • Waterfall: waterfall options, grouped shading and point tooltips.
  • Histogram and Boxplot: distribution options.
  • Heatmap Matrix: Category is the leaf X level, Group is its optional parent, and Rows / split by is the Y field. Category, Group and Row label sections format those three roles independently. Group shaded areas, separator color/thickness, multiples, shared Data labels and the normal Legend controls are supported; the unrelated Value axis section is hidden.
  • Heatmap Calendar: Category is a date and weekdays are derived as rows. It fills the available width and adapts to one or many years. Category-axis controls format/space month labels; Row labels format/space weekdays; Group labels control year visibility, color and vertical position. Optional month outlines, separated month blocks/month spacing, today and whole-current-week outlines are available.
  • Treemap: hierarchical layout, group borders and chart size. Category content is controlled by Data labels, not a separate category-label selector. Group content uses Group labels.
  • Gauge: responsive gauge arrangement and maximum gauge count (default six).
  • Pie and Doughnut: category/data and group-label formatting, and chart size.

Treemap, Gauge, Pie and Doughnut have no normal axes: axis groups are hidden and category text is configured through Data labels. Theme colors control plotted shapes independently of label font colors. Plot geometry adapts to the available chart area when the editor or tile changes size; editor-only adjustment handles are omitted from the finished visual.

For Scatter, Size by in Data is the chart-wide default. Select an individual series in Scatter / plot only when that series needs a different Size by field; choosing the default there keeps the global binding.

docs.title: Edit from Canvas
docs.text:
Select a chart tile and use Chart properties > Property group for small changes without opening Chart Web. Chart settings, Title settings (including editable title text), Plot margins, axes, labels, legend and applicable chart groups are exposed here. Use canvas theme, chart background, gridlines and the other quick controls update the stored specification and redraw the tile immediately; reopening the designer is not required.

Click a plotted bar/point to select Data labels, an x-axis to select Category axis, a y-axis to select Value axis, or the top plot border to select Plot margins. Right-click provides Chart options and available property groups. Open the full designer when changing the data configuration or needing the complete preview.

Return to Statistics and charts in Query Tool.

docs.title: Mini DAX and measures
docs.text:
Mini DAX is QReports' focused expression engine for measures and calculated columns. The Measures ribbon command and the Canvas Measures command open the WebView Measure workspace. It is used by matrices, charts, Canvas visuals, and QReports table output. It is not the same thing as sending a full DAX query to the Excel Power Pivot model.

The workspace places source Fields on the left, saved measures/calculated columns beside them, and the name, expandable expression editor, validation status, matrix wells, and result preview in the main area. The two list panes and matrix result can be resized or collapsed. Load data runs the source query with its current QReports parameters; measures remain editable before data is loaded.

The expression editor provides syntax highlighting, autocomplete, keyboard indentation and a function helper, with a docked, searchable and resizable function reference. Choosing a helper function inserts its syntax at the cursor. Drag fields into Rows, at most one Columns field, and Values to test the calculation as a crosstab. Number formats and matrix visibility are saved with each measure. The workspace follows the selected QReports application theme.

Use brackets around field or measure names containing spaces, periods, or other punctuation. Autocomplete adds the brackets automatically when needed:

YEAR([player.birthdate])
DATEDIFF([Player birth date], TODAY(), YEAR)

When the Query Web connection is model, it can run normal model queries. The formulas on this page are the smaller Mini DAX formulas managed in Measure workspace.

docs.title: Manage, rename, and audit measures
docs.text:
The header keeps the common actions visible: New, Rename, Functions, Validate, Save, Delete, and Return measures. Open New and choose Measure for a filter-context result or Calculated column for one result per source row. Less-frequent commands—Insert color value, Duplicate, Audit all, Find unused, and Load data—are grouped under Tools. Measures can be organized into folders and subfolders.

Use Tools > Insert color value to choose a theme role or a fixed manual color, preview it, and insert the quoted value at the current expression selection. Theme values such as "theme:accent" adapt with the Qanvas theme; a hex value such as "#4f6ee8" remains fixed. To create a reusable conditional-formatting color measure, right-click a source field and choose fields_pickcolor · Color switch. The generated text measure reads the field with FIRST, defines editable color variables, and returns the appropriate theme role or hex value through SWITCH(TRUE(), ...).

Use Validate for the selected formula. Use Audit all to check every measure and calculated column for invalid syntax, missing fields, and references to missing or renamed measures. The audit shows its progress through the list and reports each item that needs attention.

Use Find unused to mark cleanup candidates. A measure is marked only when no other formula references it and no object in the current Qanvas document uses it. This includes supported table, matrix, chart, card, Report Grid, rich-text/SVG, selector, filter, sort, and linked-source references. Click a result to open the measure, review it, and delete it manually if it is no longer needed. Calculated columns are excluded because they can also be consumed as ordinary source fields. The command requires the Measure workspace to be opened from Qanvas; without document context, it does not mark anything.

Use Rename when changing an existing measure name. It updates references in other measure formulas and in supported Canvas objects. If the Name field is changed directly and Save is selected, the workspace asks whether the change should be treated as a rename so dependent references are not silently broken. When the workspace was opened from Canvas, Return measures sends the updated collection back so Canvas references can be reviewed and updated together.

The reference checker is intentionally stricter than a single preview calculation: a formula can produce a value in one test context while still containing a reference that will fail elsewhere. Run Audit all before a release when measures have been renamed or removed.

docs.title: Measure or calculated column?
docs.text:
Type Evaluation context Typical use Measure Evaluated after dimensions and filters establish a group. Totals, averages, ratios, prior-period values, rank. Calculated column Evaluated once for each source row before grouping. Categories, cleaned text, date parts, row calculations.

Calculated columns cannot reference aggregate measures and cannot call aggregate or context functions such as SUM, CALCULATE, ALL, or REMOVEFILTERS.

A measure deliberately does not turn a bare row-level field reference into an implicit FIRST. State the intended aggregation so the result remains predictable when the filter context contains more than one row. FIRST and LAST accept row-level expressions, so this is valid:

FIRST(DATEPART("day", dateevent))

docs.title: Basic syntax
docs.text:
The editor stores the output name separately from the formula. For a measure named Margin, enter:

DIVIDE(SUM(Profit), SUM(Revenue))

Mini DAX supports arithmetic, comparisons, AND, OR, variables, and comments:

VAR _revenue = SUM(Revenue)
VAR _profit = SUM(Profit)
RETURN
    IF(_revenue = 0, BLANK(), DIVIDE(_profit, _revenue))

Comments begin with //. Names are matched without case sensitivity. Use Ctrl+Space or begin typing to display available names.

docs.title: Aggregate functions
docs.text:
Function Syntax Description SUM SUM(column [, filter]) Sum numeric values in context. AVERAGE / AVG AVERAGE(column [, filter]) Average numeric values. MIN MIN(column [, filter]) Minimum value. MAX MAX(column [, filter]) Maximum value. COUNT COUNT(column [, filter]) Count non-blank values. DISTINCTCOUNT DISTINCTCOUNT(column) Count distinct non-blank values. FIRST FIRST(expression [, filter]) Evaluate an expression for each row and return the first non-blank result. LAST LAST(expression [, filter]) Evaluate an expression for each row and return the last non-blank result. SELECTEDVALUE SELECTEDVALUE(column [, alternate]) Single value in context, otherwise alternate or blank.

Charts evaluate a selected measure in each plotted cell/group. For example, a heatmap using AVERAGE(temperature) displays and scales the per-cell average; it does not sum already-calculated averages.

An optional aggregate filter is a simple row condition:

SUM(Revenue, Month = 1)

docs.title: Math and ranking
docs.text:
Function Syntax Description DIVIDE DIVIDE(numerator, denominator) Safe division; zero returns blank. ROUND ROUND(number, digits) Round halves away from zero. ROUNDUP ROUNDUP(number, digits) Round away from zero. ROUNDDOWN ROUNDDOWN(number, digits) Round towards zero. NEGATE / NEG NEGATE(number) Reverse the sign. REVERSE_SIGN REVERSE_SIGN(number) Synonym for NEGATE. RANK RANK(value [, ASC|DESC] [, DENSE|SKIP]) Rank the aggregated matrix values.

RANK runs after aggregation:

RANK(Sales_total, DESC, DENSE)

docs.title: Logical functions
docs.text:
Function Syntax Description IF IF(condition, trueValue [, falseValue]) Return one of two expressions. SWITCH SWITCH(expression, value1, result1, ... [, else]) Choose from alternatives. BLANK BLANK() Return a blank value. TRUE TRUE() Logical true. FALSE FALSE() Logical false. 
SWITCH(
    TRUE(),
    Margin < 0, "Loss",
    Margin < 0.1, "Low",
    Margin < 0.25, "Medium",
    "High"
)

docs.title: Text functions
docs.text:
Function Syntax FORMAT FORMAT(value, "format") CONCATENATE CONCATENATE(value1, value2, ...) CONCATVALUES CONCATVALUES(column [, separator, maxCount, distinct]) CONTAINSSTRING CONTAINSSTRING(text, findText) UPPER UPPER(text) LOWER LOWER(text) LEFT LEFT(text, count) RIGHT RIGHT(text, count) MID MID(text, start, count) CAST CAST(value, "type")

MID uses a one-based start. The & operator can also concatenate text. CAST target types are quoted strings: "DATE", "DATETIME", "TEXT", "INTEGER", "NUMBER", or "BOOLEAN".

CAST(_month, "INTEGER")

CONCATENATE(UPPER(Region), " - ", FORMAT(SUM(Sales), "#,##0"))

docs.title: Date functions
docs.text:
Function Syntax Description YEAR YEAR(date) Extract year. MONTH MONTH(date) Extract month. DAY DAY(date) Extract day of month. WEEK WEEK(date) ISO-style week number: Monday-first, with the first four-day week as week 1. TODAY TODAY() Current local date. DATEDIFF DATEDIFF(startDate, endDate, interval) Whole elapsed years, months, or days. Use YEAR, MONTH, or DAY; quoted interval names are also accepted. DATEPART DATEPART("part", date) Extract year, quarter, month, day, day-of-year, week, weekday, hour, minute, or second. Quote the part name. DATEFROMPARTS DATEFROMPARTS(year, month, day) Construct a date. DATEOFFSET DATEOFFSET(date, years, months, days, weeks) Shift a date.

Calculated-column examples:

DATEPART("week", "2026-10-12")

The example above returns week 42. DATEPART("week", date) uses the same week calculation as WEEK(date). Other valid part names include "year", "quarter", "month", "day", "dayofyear", "weekday", "hour", "minute", and "second".

DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(InvoiceDate), MONTH(InvoiceDate), 1)

DATEOFFSET(InvoiceDate, -1, 0, 0, 0)

For completed age in years:

DATEDIFF([player.birthdate], TODAY(), YEAR)

docs.title: Filter context with CALCULATE
docs.text:
CALCULATE reevaluates a supported aggregate after changing simple column filters:

CALCULATE(SUM(Cost), Year = 2025)

Use REMOVEFILTERS or ALL inside CALCULATE to remove selected dimension filters:

VAR _currentYear = MAX(Year)
RETURN
    CALCULATE(
        SUM(Cost),
        REMOVEFILTERS(Year),
        Year = _currentYear - 1
    )

Here, ALL(column) and REMOVEFILTERS(column) only remove that column's current filter inside CALCULATE; they do not return general-purpose DAX table expressions.

docs.title: Parameters in formulas
docs.text:
QReports patches parameter tokens before compiling a formula:

CALCULATE(
    SUM(Revenue),
    Year = {{pyear}}
)

Use a raw numeric parameter for pyear. For text comparisons, use DAX string parsing or provide quotes through the parameter definition.

The Measures workspace shows canvas parameters in Functions and suggests them when {{ is typed in the expression editor. Validation, matrix testing, chart rendering, presentation, and webpage rendering all resolve the current parameter value through the same formula path.

docs.title: Average price
docs.text:
VAR _amount = SUM(Amount)
VAR _quantity = SUM(Quantity)
RETURN DIVIDE(_amount, _quantity)

docs.title: Growth percentage
docs.text:
IF(
    PriorYear = 0,
    BLANK(),
    DIVIDE(CurrentYear - PriorYear, PriorYear)
)

docs.title: Row-level category
docs.text:
Create a calculated column and enter:

IF(Amount < 0, "Credit", "Debit")

docs.title: Differences from full DAX
docs.text:
Mini DAX is intentionally smaller than Microsoft DAX:

  • it evaluates QReports visual data, not a single canvas-wide semantic model; Qanvas tables, matrices, and charts can resolve a measure from a directly linked source, while dimension relationships expose linked fields to table groups, matrix axes, and chart categories/groups;
  • it is an expression engine, not the DAX query language—EVALUATE and DEFINE belong to model mode;
  • iterator and table functions such as SUMX, FILTER, ADDCOLUMNS, SUMMARIZE, and RELATED are not implemented;
  • there is no transitive relationship propagation, general-purpose cross-source DAX, or Power Pivot storage engine;
  • CALCULATE supports focused column comparisons plus ALL/REMOVEFILTERS, not every DAX filter expression;
  • time-intelligence functions such as SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR, DATESYTD, and DAX DATEADD are not included; use DATEOFFSET and explicit filters;
  • RANK is a QReports post-aggregation operation, not RANKX;
  • blanks use an internal representation and may render as empty output;
  • number, week, and date formatting can depend on the current Windows culture.

Use a Qanvas source relationship when a matrix only needs a prepared measure from another source at a shared grain such as Company + Period. If a formula requires arbitrary model relationships, iterators, or advanced time intelligence, use a real Power Pivot measure instead. Query Tool's Power Pivot menu links to Excel's model tools.

Physical source columns retain their exact names, including underscores. Names such as accounts_receivable, work_in_progress, and budget_revenue are valid Mini DAX field references; only recognized terminal aggregate aliases such as _avg, _min, and _max are reduced to their base field by legacy matrix mapping.

Return to the Query Tool guide.

docs.title: Formula Helper
docs.text:
Formula Helper is the reference and code-generation pane for QRep Excel Code. It helps you find a keyword, supply valid options, preview the resulting syntax, and insert it into Excel.

It is not intended to be the primary tutorial for the language. Start with QRep Excel Code to understand how connection, query, and output rows work together, then use Formula Helper while building a report.

docs.title: Open the helper
docs.text: Choose QRep > Formula Helper to show or hide the pane on the right side of Excel. The pane stays close to the worksheet so you can inspect a report definition and insert generated code at the active cell.

docs.title: Choose what to create
docs.text:
The workflow selector organizes the supported builders into four groups.

Mode Available templates Report output Table, Dynamic table, Pivot table, Summary, Subtotal Companion row Column / measure row, Crossfilter row, Parameter row Control setup Parameter setting, Template report setup, Sheet password Raw keyword Direct access to the available keyword definitions

Selecting a template displays a short explanation, a structure preview, and only the options relevant to that keyword.

docs.title: Look up reference information
docs.text:
Use the reference browser and search box when you need to check a function, option, filter operator, or example. This is the quickest use of Formula Helper: look up the exact syntax without leaving Excel or changing the current worksheet definition.

The helper can also load the active Excel definition, making it easier to inspect or adjust code that is already present.

docs.title: Generate report output code
docs.text:
The output builders produce correctly ordered options for:

  • table, including group, filter, sort, options, and top rows;
  • dtable, for structured Excel table output;
  • ptable, for pivot-style output;
  • summary, for compact value and measure rows;
  • subtotal, including groups, filters, sorting, and outline options.

For example, selecting Report output > Dynamic table and entering a group, filter, and row limit can produce:

dtable;group(continent);filter(year=2026);toprows(20)

The generated syntax is shown in the preview before it is inserted.

docs.title: Table helper
docs.text:
The dedicated table helper is designed for complete table definitions, not only the first keyword cell. Use it to:

  • choose output fields and their order;
  • assign aggregations and display labels;
  • create an explicit header row;
  • create footer values such as $sum, $count, and $avg;
  • add footer labels and outline behavior;
  • preview the worksheet structure before insertion.

An inserted template can look like this:

ABCD 7table;group(continent)continentpopulation 8+headerCONTINENTPOPULATION 9+footer;outlinelabel(SUMMARY)$sum

docs.title: Subtotal helper
docs.text:
Use the subtotal helper to generate hierarchical output without manually assembling every template row. It supports grouping levels, selected measures, labels, headers and footers, Excel outline behavior, and initially collapsed groups.

Preview the structure before insertion. Check that the grouping order runs from the outer group to the detailed level and that aggregate values are placed in the intended output columns.

docs.title: Companion rows
docs.text:
The Column / measure row builder supports field or measure names, filters, aggregation, units, labels, and options. Its aggregation choices include SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, FIRST, and LAST.

The Crossfilter row builder creates per-column filters. The Parameter row builder creates parameter/value pairs for report code.

docs.title: Control-sheet setup
docs.text:
The Control setup mode generates rows intended for _control:

Template Generated purpose Parameter setting set | parameter | value | user input | advanced JSON Template report setup setreport | template | report | parameter/value pairs Sheet password setpassword | sheet | password

For advanced parameter input types, list lookups, tree levels, formatting, text parsing, and sheet scope, use Parameter Manager after creating the base setting. See Parameters.

docs.title: Insert safely
docs.text:
1. Select the target cell or existing definition in Excel.
  2. Choose the mode and template.
  3. Fill in the displayed options.
  4. Review the syntax or worksheet preview.
  5. Use Insert into Excel only after confirming the active position.
  6. Load the selected line to test the result.

Use Load from Excel when modifying an existing definition. This reduces the risk of recreating options that are already stored in the worksheet.

docs.title: Run a query
docs.text:
1. Open Excel and select the QReports ribbon.
  2. Open the Query Tool.
  3. Select or configure a connection.
  4. Enter a query and preview the result.
  5. Return the result to the active workbook.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Learn how the worksheet definition is assembled in QRep Excel Code.
  • Use Formula Helper to look up syntax and generate table or subtotal code.
  • Use Mini SQL to query Excel tables without an external database.
  • Add parameters to make a report interactive.
  • Add Mini DAX measures or calculated columns before returning data.
  • Save the workbook with its QReports definitions.

docs.title: Qvitr Enterprise installer
docs.text:
The recommended Windows package is Qvitr Enterprise. It installs Qanvas and, when selected, the Excel and PowerPoint integrations. The installer also supplies the required .NET 8 Desktop Runtime when it is missing.

  1. Close Qanvas, Excel and PowerPoint.
  2. Download Qvitr-enterprise-setup.exe from the latest Qvitr GitHub release.
  3. Run the setup as an administrator and select the required components.
  4. Open Qanvas or Office and verify the Qvitr commands are available.

docs.title: Manual updates
docs.text:
Qvitr does not check for enterprise updates automatically. Choose Check for updates from:

  • Qanvas: Help (?) > Check for updates;
  • Excel: QRep > Settings > Check for updates;
  • PowerPoint: QReports > Help > Check for updates.

Qvitr compares the installed Qanvas file version with the latest release manifest. When a newer release exists, it asks before downloading. The download is checked against its SHA-256 hash and must contain an Authenticode signature before Windows setup is opened. Close Qanvas, Excel and PowerPoint before confirming the installation so their installed files are not locked.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Microsoft Excel for Windows
  • .NET Framework 4.8
  • Visual Studio Tools for Office Runtime

docs.title: Install QReports
docs.text:
1. Close Excel.
  2. Download and run setup.exe.
  3. Complete the installation prompts.
  4. Open Excel and confirm that the QReports ribbon is visible.

The legacy ClickOnce Excel package checks its installation site for published updates. This is separate from the manual Qvitr Enterprise update command.

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text: For Qvitr Enterprise, use Check for updates manually. For the legacy ClickOnce installation, close and reopen Excel after a release and follow its ClickOnce prompt if one appears.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Add a separate List tile for operational, editable rows. Keep Table as a simple read-only detail view and Matrix as the analytical table. Do not remove or silently convert the current Table tile: existing reports depend on its saved shape, and editing introduces permissions, validation, row identity, and write-back semantics that a reporting table should not acquire implicitly.

The three tiles then have clear jobs:

Tile Primary job Data behavior Matrix Grouped analysis, pivots, subtotals, drill and hierarchy Read-only Table Fast flat detail and export Read-only List Task lists and small operational registers Editable when embedded; linked sources are read-only initially

Table and Matrix should continue to share rendering, formatting, sorting and field-picking code where practical. A later release may present Table as a "Flat table" preset of the Matrix renderer, but the saved kind: "table" must remain supported. Conversion should be explicit: Convert to Matrix or Create editable List snapshot.

docs.title: Reuse the existing data model
docs.text:
Qanvas already has embedded/manual tables with typed columns, cell editing, lookups, calendar input, column resize/reorder, and automatic row creation. The List tile should be a focused view and workflow on top of that capability, not a second row database.

Two modes are recommended:

  • Embedded list creates a private embedded manual source owned by the tile. The source contains the canonical schema and rows. An Expose as datasource option gives it a user-facing name and makes it available to cards, charts, matrices, filters, and other pages. The data is not copied when it is exposed.
  • Linked source references an existing Qanvas source. SQL, API, workbook, and generated rows remain read-only because they require a real write-back contract. A linked view may opt into editing when its source is another embedded List/manual table; every linked view then edits the same canonical rows instead of a cached copy.

This is slightly different from the Gantt tile's tile-owned task array and published gantt:<tile-id> proxy. For a generic List, source-first ownership is cleaner because its data is already ordinary rows. The tile stores view and editing preferences; the embedded source stores rows and schema.

Suggested stable identity:

{
  "kind": "list",
  "sourceId": "list:8ee41e2a",
  "list": {
    "storage": "embedded",
    "exposeAsDatasource": true,
    "datasourceName": "Project actions",
    "columns": [
      { "field": "title", "width": { "mode": "percent", "value": 35 } },
      { "field": "status", "width": { "mode": "px", "value": 140 } },
      { "field": "due_at", "width": { "mode": "auto" } }
    ],
    "allowPresentEditing": false
  }
}

The embedded source descriptor should carry ownerTileId and a stable source ID. Deleting or unpublishing it must warn about dependent visuals. A List must not consume its own published alias.

docs.title: Default task-list schema
docs.text:
Start with a useful but small template. Users can remove optional fields or add their own.

Field Type Behavior id UUID/text Immutable primary key; hidden by default line_no Integer Automatic display/order number title Short text Required primary description description Long text Optional multiline editor status Choice Open, In progress, Completed priority Choice Low, Normal, High owner Text or lookup Optional assignee due_at Date Shared date picker completed_at Date/time Optional; may be set when completed created_at Date/time Automatic, read-only updated_at Date/time Automatic, read-only

created_by and updated_by should only appear when the host supplies a stable user identity. Otherwise they imply an audit trail that Qanvas cannot prove.

Custom field types for version one:

  • Short text and long/multiline text
  • Integer, decimal, currency and percent
  • Boolean
  • Date and date/time, stored as ISO values
  • Choice with separate stored code and displayed label
  • Lookup with source, key field, display field, missing-value behavior and an optional manual code/label list

URL, email, attachments, formulas, cascading lookups and write-back adapters fit later phases. A lookup stores the code; it never stores the display text as the authoritative value. Date fields use the existing shared calendar.

docs.title: List workflow
docs.text:
• Add row creates a row below the current row. Enter commits the cell; Tab moves across fields and creates another row from the final editable cell.
  • Choice and lookup cells use a searchable dropdown. Date cells use the shared date picker. Long text can expand into a resizable editor while retaining an inline preview.
  • Required fields, numeric ranges, duplicate keys and missing lookup values are validated at cell and row level. Invalid rows remain visible and explain the error; they are not silently discarded.
  • Row commands are Duplicate, Delete, Move, Mark complete and Open details. Delete and schema/type conversions remain undoable or require confirmation.
  • Search, sort, filters, frozen columns and compact/comfortable row density use the same shared grid behavior as Table and embedded manual tables.
  • Column width is { mode: "auto" | "px" | "percent", value? }. Percent widths share the available area, pixel widths remain fixed, and Auto consumes the remainder with sensible minimums. Multiline rows can use Auto height or a configurable fixed/clamped height.

Editing is enabled in normal Edit mode. Presentation editing is a separate, off-by-default option, matching Gantt. Web export should remain read-only until there is an explicit persistence target.

docs.title: Designer
docs.text:
Use the established two-pane designer: properties on the left and a real live preview on the right. The dialog is movable and resizable. Compact group shortcuts remain visible above the property pane:

  • Data — Embedded/Linked mode, source, expose/name datasource
  • Fields — add/reorder fields, type, required/default value, lookup setup
  • Layout — widths, row height, density, multiline, frozen columns
  • Appearance — theme roles, header/cell typography, borders, badges
  • Interaction — add/delete/duplicate, Present editing, selection behavior

Preview objects are navigation targets:

  • Click a column heading to focus that field and its width settings.
  • Click a value cell to focus that field's editor and formatting.
  • Click the toolbar, row action area, empty state or list frame to focus Interaction, Layout or Appearance respectively.
  • Keyboard focus moves to the selected property section, and the active preview target and shortcut use the same highlighted state.

There is no Apply/Save button in the designer. Every valid change updates the tile/source model and preview immediately and participates in canvas Undo/Redo. Closing the designer only closes it. The document still uses the normal Qanvas Save command to persist the .qanvas file, so live designer updates do not pretend that the file has already been written to disk.

docs.title: Form view and inspector reuse
docs.text:
The List tile also has a Form · one record view. This is a view of the same source and schema, not a second data store or a separate tile type. It is suited to test-case registration, issue intake, master-data maintenance, and any case where a wide row is easier to edit as a professional form.

  • The form supports 1–6 columns. Each column can use Auto, relative percent, or fixed pixel width. Row and column gaps and compact spacing are configurable.
  • Every visible field has column, column span, and row span. Labels can be above or to the left of controls.
  • Automatic controls follow the field type: date/date-time picker, checkbox, choice/lookup select, URL picker, numeric input, and multiline text.
  • Numeric fields can opt into a slider with min/max/step. Choice, lookup, and numeric values can opt into a badge when a display-only summary is preferred.
  • A navigator moves through the records that remain after source, page, and tile filters. Add, duplicate, and delete use the same permissions as the normal List view.
  • selectedRecordId is stable when rows are sorted or filtered. With followSelection, clicking a row in a table List updates Form views using the same source, including a form on another page when that page is opened.

An inspector should be a presentation shell around this same form schema. It may be docked to the side or bottom, floating and movable, or opened on demand, but should not own its own rows or duplicate field configuration. An optional future Use form as inspector action can select a Form-view List definition and choose its placement. This keeps ad-hoc layout power while avoiding a second implementation of typed editors, validation, theming, and persistence.

docs.title: Delivery plan
docs.text:
1. Add kind: "list", the embedded-source owner metadata, the task-list template, linked read-only mode, and datasource exposure.
  2. Reuse the manual-table cell editors for typed fields, lookup/manual lists, date picker, multiline text, widths, validation and inline row creation.
  3. Add the movable/resizable designer, property shortcuts, clickable preview, keyboard flow, Undo/Redo and Present-mode permission.
  4. Add search/filter/frozen-column polish, conversion commands and regression coverage for save/load, published-source dependencies and exports.
  5. Only after migration coverage is complete, consider hiding Add Table in favor of a Matrix flat-table preset. Continue rendering existing Table tiles.

This approach has moderate implementation risk: most difficult primitives already exist, while the new work is ownership, UX composition, validation, conversion and lifecycle handling rather than another storage engine.

docs.title: Local queries and data
docs.text: Local data lets Qanvas and Query Tool work with manually entered tables, imported files, web files, saved remote-query results, and combinations of those sources without requiring a live database for every operation.

docs.title: Local source types
docs.text:
Badge Type Meaning M Manual Rows entered and maintained locally. F File Imported CSV, text, or Excel data. W Web file File data imported from a remembered URL. V Source view A saved SQL or API query materialized as local rows. C Combined source A Mini SQL result built from local tables or views.

Choose local — Local JSONL tables in Query Tool. Groups act like schemas, so qualified names such as [weather].[Temperature] or weather.Temperature can be used in previews, joins, and Mini SQL.

docs.title: Create and refresh local results
docs.text:
Use Save as source view to preserve a remote SQL/API definition and its local result. Use Save as combined source for a reusable query across local tables and views. A source view refresh reruns its remote query; a combined-source refresh recalculates from its local dependencies.

Update sources shows age and status and refreshes selected sources in dependency order. Refresh upstream views before combined results. Missing dependencies and cycles must be corrected before the chain can run.

docs.title: Imports and preparation steps
docs.text:
CSV, text, Excel, and web imports can remember their source, comments, renamed or removed columns, types, and removed rows. Reopening or reimporting the source replays the remaining preparation steps. These steps prepare the table before a Mini SQL query consumes it.

Local rows and definitions are stored on the computer or packaged with a portable Qanvas report where supported. Credentials remain external and should be managed through named connections and SecretManager.

Continue with the complete Query Tool local-source reference or the Mini SQL guide.

docs.title: Mini SQL for Excel tables
docs.text:
Mini SQL is QReports' in-memory query language for Excel tables and delimited files. It provides a familiar SQL-shaped way to filter, join, group, calculate, and sort tabular data without first loading it into an external database.

Mini SQL is used when Conn is set to table and for saved CSV/TEXT file connections. The same engine is also used for published Canvas tables.

In Query Web, local manual/imported tables, saved source views and combined sources also use this SQL-shaped workflow. Update sources refreshes remote source views before dependent combined sources; manual tables are snapshots and are not refresh candidates.

docs.title: First query
docs.text:
Assume the workbook contains Excel tables named country and continent:

SELECT
    continent,
    SUM(population) AS population_total
FROM country
WHERE year = 2025
GROUP BY continent
ORDER BY population_total DESC

To run it:

  1. Open Query Tool.
  2. Select table from Conn.
  3. Select Table to list workbook tables.
  4. Enter the Mini SQL statement.
  5. Select Run or press F5.

Table and column names come from Excel table names and headers, not worksheet names or cell addresses.

docs.title: Supported statement shape
docs.text:
Mini SQL supports one SELECT statement with the following general shape:

SELECT [TOP number]
    expression [AS alias], ...
FROM table [alias]
[INNER | LEFT | RIGHT | FULL [OUTER]] JOIN table [alias] ON condition
[WHERE condition]
[GROUP BY column, ...]
[HAVING condition]
[ORDER BY expression [ASC | DESC], ...]

Supported query features include:

  • SELECT * for ordinary, non-aggregated projections;
  • column aliases with AS;
  • table aliases;
  • TOP n;
  • inner, left, right, and full joins;
  • WHERE comparisons using =, <>, <, >, <=, and >=;
  • AND, OR, IN (...), BETWEEN, LIKE, IS NULL, and IS NOT NULL;
  • GROUP BY, aggregate expressions, and HAVING;
  • ORDER BY ... ASC and ORDER BY ... DESC;
  • CASE WHEN ... THEN ... ELSE ... END;
  • QReports parameters such as {{pyear}}.

With grouping or aggregate expressions, list every required non-aggregate output column in GROUP BY. SELECT * is not supported in an aggregate query.

docs.title: Joins and aliases
docs.text:
Aliases make joins easier to read and prevent ambiguous column names:

SELECT
    c.country_name,
    c.continent_code,
    g.continent_name,
    c.population
FROM country c
LEFT JOIN continent g
    ON c.continent_code = g.continent_code
WHERE c.population > 1000000
ORDER BY c.population DESC

Join conditions should use column equality or other straightforward comparisons. Mini SQL is intended for table-shaped reporting logic; highly nested database join expressions should remain in the source database.

docs.title: Filters and parameters
docs.text:
SELECT country_name, year, population
FROM country
WHERE year BETWEEN 2020 AND 2025
  AND continent_code IN ('EU', 'NA')
  AND country_name LIKE 'N%'
  AND population IS NOT NULL

String literals use single quotes. A single quote inside a value is doubled: 'O''Brien'.

Parameters are resolved before Mini SQL runs:

SELECT country_name, population
FROM country
WHERE year = {{pyear}}
  AND {{continent}}

If continent produces continent IN ('Europe','Asia'), the parsed statement is valid Mini SQL. Use Query > Parse query to inspect the exact result.

docs.title: Aggregate functions
docs.text:
Function Syntax Purpose COUNT COUNT(column) Count non-null values. COUNTDISTINCT COUNTDISTINCT(column) Count distinct non-null values. SUM SUM(column) Sum numeric values. AVG AVG(column) Average numeric values. MIN MIN(column) Minimum value. MAX MAX(column) Maximum value. CONCAT CONCAT(column [, delimiter]) Join unique text values; comma is the default delimiter. 
SELECT
    continent,
    COUNTDISTINCT(country_code) AS countries,
    SUM(population) AS population,
    CONCAT(country_name, ', ') AS country_list
FROM country
GROUP BY continent
HAVING SUM(population) > 100000000
ORDER BY population DESC

docs.title: String functions
docs.text:
Function Syntax Example SUBSTRING SUBSTRING(text, start, length) SUBSTRING(country_name, 1, 3) LENGTH LENGTH(text) LENGTH(country_name) REPLACE REPLACE(text, find, replacement) REPLACE(code, '-', '') TRIM TRIM(text) TRIM(country_name) LEFT LEFT(text, length) LEFT(account, 3) RIGHT RIGHT(text, length) RIGHT(account, 2) UPPER UPPER(text) UPPER(country_name) LOWER LOWER(text) LOWER(country_name) FORMAT FORMAT(value, format) FORMAT(amount, '#,##0.00')

SUBSTRING uses a one-based start position. FORMAT returns text and uses the current Windows culture.

docs.title: Date functions
docs.text:
Function Syntax Notes GETDATE GETDATE() Current local date and time. TODAY TODAY() Current local date with no time. XLDATE XLDATE(value) Convert an Excel serial value to a date. XLDATETIME XLDATETIME(value) Convert an Excel serial value to date and time. DATEADD DATEADD(interval, number, date) Adds an interval; fractional numbers truncate and month ends clamp. DATEDIFF DATEDIFF(interval, date1, date2) Integer date-part boundaries crossed, not fractional elapsed time. YEAR YEAR(date) Extract the year. MONTH MONTH(date) Extract the month number. WEEK WEEK(date) Same as DATEPART(week,date). ISOWEEK ISOWEEK(date) ISO week number 1-53; weeks start Monday, and week 1 contains January 4. Same as DATEPART(iso_week,date). DATEPART DATEPART(part, date) Extract a date part, including ISO week.

The interval/part accepts both bare keywords and quoted strings: DATEADD(d,7,t.date) and DATEADD('d',7,t.date) are equivalent. Aliases are case-insensitive.

Part Accepted aliases Year year, yy, yyyy, y Quarter quarter, qq, q Month month, mm, m Day day, dd, d Day of year dayofyear, dy Week week, wk, ww Weekday weekday, dw, wd, w Hour hour, hh, h Minute minute, mi, n Second second, ss, s Millisecond millisecond, ms ISO week (DATEPART only) iso_week, isowk, isoww

DATEPART(week,date) and WEEK(date) use Sunday-first weeks with January 1 in week 1. DATEPART(weekday,date) returns Sunday = 1 through Saturday = 7. MiniSQL does not support SET DATEFIRST. Use DATEPART(iso_week,date) for Monday-first ISO week numbering. This replaces the previous Monday/first-four-day behavior of DATEPART(week,...).

DATEDIFF counts boundaries: from 23:59:59 to midnight is 1 day, 1 hour, 1 minute and 1 second. Week differences count Sunday boundaries. Year, quarter and month differences count calendar boundaries, not complete elapsed periods. Results are signed 32-bit integers; overflow is an error. This replaces the previous elapsed-time day/hour/minute/second calculation. DATEADD(weekday,...) adds calendar days, not working days. This follows SQL Server boundary semantics.

Compatibility aliases y (year), h (hour), wd/w (weekday) are retained. Unlike SQL Server's y, MiniSQL's legacy y means year; use dy or dayofyear for day of year. NULL arguments return NULL. Dates, date strings and numeric Excel serial dates are supported. MONTH(date) returns 1-12.

FORMAT(value,'pattern') uses system culture and .NET numeric/date patterns. Prefer yyyy-MM for year/month. Excel-style lowercase month tokens are also accepted in date-only patterns: FORMAT(t.date,'yyyy-mm') returns, for example, 2026-09. In a time pattern such as yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm, uppercase MM means month and lowercase mm means minutes. The query option to disable FORMAT returns the original value instead of text.

SELECT
    invoice_date,
    YEAR(invoice_date) AS invoice_year,
    DATEADD(month, 1, invoice_date) AS next_month,
    FORMAT(invoice_date, 'yyyy-MM-dd') AS date_text
FROM invoices

docs.title: Logical, numeric, and conversion functions
docs.text:
Function Syntax Purpose CASE CASE WHEN condition THEN value ELSE value END Conditional output. IIF IIF(condition, trueValue, falseValue) Inline condition. COALESCE COALESCE(value1, value2, ...) First non-null value. ISNULL ISNULL(value, replacement) Replace a null. ROUND ROUND(number, decimals) Round to decimal places. FLOOR FLOOR(number) Round down. CEILING CEILING(number) Round up. ABS ABS(number) Absolute value. MOD MOD(dividend, divisor) Division remainder. CAST CAST(expression, 'datatype') Convert to a supported type.

Supported CAST targets include integer, long, double, decimal, text, date, datetime, and Boolean aliases. Mini SQL uses CAST(value, 'INT'), not SQL Server's CAST(value AS INT) syntax.

CONVERT may appear in function-help metadata in some builds, but the Mini SQL evaluator currently implements CAST. Prefer CAST for portable QReports definitions.

docs.title: Differences from database SQL
docs.text:
Mini SQL deliberately does not try to be a full database server:

  • it operates on in-memory table data and has no database indexes or query optimizer;
  • it supports one SELECT, not INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE, or stored procedures;
  • CTEs, subqueries, UNION, window functions, and database-specific syntax are not supported;
  • use TOP n; LIMIT and OFFSET are not part of the parser;
  • schema-qualified database names are not relevant to workbook table mode;
  • function coverage and null/type conversion rules are smaller than in a database;
  • very large workbooks can use substantial memory because source tables are materialized;
  • culture can affect text-to-number, date parsing, and FORMAT output;
  • database permissions, transactions, indexes, and execution plans do not apply.

Use Mini SQL when the source is already in Excel and the transformation is report-sized. Use a named database connection when the source is large, the SQL is complex, or filtering and aggregation should happen on the server.

docs.title: Performance and limits
docs.text:
MiniSQL keeps the native types of source columns in simple projections and joins. A single-table query reads the original table without making an alias copy. For a simple SELECT TOP n without sorting, grouping, or DISTINCT, it stops producing rows when it reaches n. SUM, AVG, MIN, and MAX return NULL when a group has no non-null values; COUNT returns zero. NULL join keys do not match each other.

Open Settings → MiniSQL limits to set maximum rows per source, maximum intermediate rows, maximum result rows, and a query timeout in seconds. A value of 0 disables each limit, which is the default for existing installations. These limits apply to local MiniSQL execution, not to queries executed by SQL Server. The source-row limit is checked after a source is loaded, so it does not prevent an oversized JSON file from being read into memory first. Timeouts are cooperative checks during MiniSQL execution, not a cancellation of source loading. Stage timings are written to the application log.

Developers can run tests/mini-sql-performance.ps1 to compare 10k, 100k, 250k, 500k, and 1m-row synthetic tables. Those results measure in-memory execution and synthetic table construction separately; they are not a JSON-file loading benchmark.

docs.title: CSV and delimited text files
docs.text:
Create a CSV or TEXT connection in Connection Manager and select the source file. Configure separator, whether the first row contains headers, and encoding. Quoted fields are supported.

The source appears using a normalized version of its filename. The stable alias data is also available, which avoids problems when a filename contains spaces or punctuation:

SELECT region, SUM(amount) AS amount
FROM data
GROUP BY region
ORDER BY amount DESC

Delimited values are initially read as text. Use the Mini SQL conversion functions when numeric or date interpretation is required, and verify separators/encoding if the preview produces an unexpected number of columns.

CSV/TXT, Excel and web imports can store a source comment and replayable preparation steps such as renamed/removed columns, data types and removed source rows. Reopening the local source restores the original location and reapplies the remaining steps. This preparation is separate from the Mini SQL query that consumes the finished local table.

Return to the Query Tool guide.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameters let users change queries, Mini SQL, Mini DAX, API definitions, charts, and Canvas content without editing the underlying text. Definitions are managed in Parameter Manager; user-enabled values appear in the simpler Parameter Input form.

docs.title: Add and order parameters
docs.text:
1. Open Parameters from the QRep Ribbon or select Param in Query Tool.
  2. Open the advanced manager if Parameter Input is shown first.
  3. Select Add.
  4. Enter the parameter name and current value.
  5. Choose an input type and configure its tabs.
  6. Check User input if report users should change it.
  7. Select Save.

Parameter names are referenced as {{name}}. Keep names short and avoid punctuation that could be confused with a property reference.

The order in Parameter Manager controls Parameter Input. Right-click the list to move a parameter Up, Down, First, or Last. The UI checkbox column identifies parameters with User input enabled; click the checkbox directly to enable or disable it.

For Manual list and SQL list parameters, Pick opens the configured selector. The popup uses single selection, checked multi-selection, or a hierarchical tree as appropriate and shows the current selection before it is applied.

docs.title: Parameter Manager layout
docs.text:
The editor is divided into tabs so that only settings relevant to the selected input type are shown:

Tab What it controls When it appears Setup Input type, user input, blank/multi-select behavior, manual values, sheet scope, list height, and expanding lists. Always. Lookup Connection, lookup query, value/display columns, and tree-level columns. List inputs; the lookup fields are required for SQL list. Text parsing Prefix/postfix, None handling, item encapsulation, and separator. Always. Format Date format or numeric minimum, maximum, increment, and number format. Date picker or Numeric input only.

The blue i buttons beside Manual list, Tree level columns, and Text parsing open short examples without changing the parameter. They are useful as an in-form syntax reference.

docs.title: Common fields
docs.text: Field Purpose Name Stable token name, for example pyear. Current value Current raw value or first selected lookup value. Default value Fallback when no current value exists. Display name Label shown to the user. Description Help text below the input control. User input Include the parameter in Parameter Input. Allow blank Permit an empty selected value. Multi select Permit more than one list value. Sheet scope Restrict visibility to selected worksheets; no selection means all sheets.

docs.title: Text
docs.text:
Use Text for free-form input such as a year, account code, or search term.

WHERE fiscal_year = {{pyear}}

For numeric text, use Raw text parsing. For a SQL text value, choose SQL string so Europe becomes 'Europe'.

docs.title: Manual list
docs.text:
Use Manual list when choices are stable and do not need a query. Enter comma-separated items, one item per line, or value/display pairs supported by the editor.

EU=Europe
NA=North America
AS=Asia

The stored value can be EU while the user sees Europe.

For a hierarchical multi-select list, enable Hierarchical tree list and enter one complete path per line. Separate levels with >; the final segment is the selectable leaf:

Europe > Western Europe > BE=Belgium
Europe > Nordics > NO=Norway
Asia > East Asia > JP=Japan

This creates Continent → Region → Country. Selecting a parent selects or clears every leaf beneath it. Any number of parent levels is supported. Existing comma-, semicolon-, and newline-separated flat lists remain valid.

For a tree, keep each complete path on its own physical line. Use value=display only on the final leaf when the stored value and caption differ. For example, NO is inserted into the query while Norway is shown to the user. Commas and semicolons are intended for flat lists, not as hierarchy markers.

docs.title: SQL list
docs.text:
Use SQL list when choices should be loaded from a connection or Excel table.

The Manual list box is disabled for SQL lists. A lookup connection and lookup SQL must be configured before the parameter can be saved.

Configure:

  • Lookup connection: named database connection, table, or another supported source;
  • Lookup SQL: query returning lookup rows;
  • Value column: value inserted into the query;
  • Display column: friendly text shown in Parameter Input;
  • Hierarchical tree list: show multiple parent levels;
  • Tree level columns: comma-separated result columns from root to parent;
  • List height: minimum height of the list control.
  • Expand height: let the multi-select list or tree use additional vertical space when Parameter Input is resized.

Example lookup:

SELECT
    Region,
    Continent,
    CountryCode,
    CountryName
FROM country
ORDER BY Continent, Region, CountryName

For Continent → Region → Country:

  • Value column: CountryCode
  • Display column: CountryName
  • Tree level columns: Continent, Region

The value/display columns form the lowest leaf. Checking or clearing a parent checks or clears all descendants. Tree selection is intended for multi-select lists.

If several parameters have Expand height enabled, only the first eligible multi-select list in Parameter Manager order expands. Parameters above it remain anchored to the top, while parameters below it remain anchored to the bottom. Reorder parameters in Parameter Manager to choose which list receives the extra space.

docs.title: Pick and verify list values
docs.text:
Select Pick... in Parameter Manager to test the configured list before saving:

  • a single-select parameter shows one selectable value;
